prompt: An administrator creates a custom theme for the marketing department in the Microsoft 365 admin center, but the Marketing security group cannot be selected on the theme's General tab. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Assign the theme to a Microsoft 365 group of marketing users
Convert the security group to a mail-enabled security group
Assign the theme to each marketing user individually
Add the security group to the default theme instead

explanation: Group themes can be mapped only to Microsoft 365 groups (up to five per theme), so the marketing users must be in a Microsoft 365 group. Security groups, mail-enabled security groups and distribution groups are not supported. Themes cannot be assigned to individual users, and the default theme applies to everyone and has no group assignment.

prompt: A company wants the logo in the Microsoft 365 navigation bar to open the corporate intranet home page when users select it. Where should a Global Administrator configure this?

options.text: Organization information on the Organization profile tab
The On-click link on the Logos page of the custom theme
A custom tile for apps on the Organization profile tab
The banner logo in Microsoft Entra company branding

explanation: The Logos page of a custom theme (Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Custom themes) has an On-click link that sets where the logo navigates; without it the logo opens the Microsoft 365 home page. Organization information holds contact details. A custom tile adds an entry to the app launcher rather than changing the logo, and the Entra banner logo appears on the sign-in page, not the navigation bar.

prompt: A tenant has a default theme and two group themes, one assigned to the Sales Microsoft 365 group and one assigned to the Field Microsoft 365 group. A user is a member of both groups. Which theme does the user see?

options.text: The Sales theme, because it was created first
The Field theme, because it was assigned most recently
The default theme
No organization theme; the Microsoft default colors are used

explanation: A user who is assigned to more than one group theme is shown the organization's default theme. Creation order and assignment order do not decide between group themes, and the user does not fall back to unbranded Microsoft colors while a default theme exists.

prompt: A company wants its logo and the label 'Managed by' to appear at the bottom of the Chat screen in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A browser-language customization in Microsoft Entra company branding
A group theme assigned to a Microsoft 365 group of Copilot users
The sign-in page text in Microsoft Entra company branding
The Copilot Chat page of the default custom theme

explanation: The branded Copilot Chat footer is configured on the Copilot Chat page of the default theme and uses the logo from that theme's Logos page, with a footer style such as 'Managed by'. The option is available for the default theme only, so a group theme cannot provide it. Microsoft Entra company branding settings affect the sign-in experience, not the Copilot app.

prompt: A company wants its own background image and banner logo to appear on the Microsoft Entra sign-in page. The task must be delegated by using the least privileged role. Which role should be assigned?

options.text: Organizational Branding Administrator
Global Reader
User Administrator
Domain Name Administrator

explanation: Organizational Branding Administrator is the minimum role required to customize company branding (Entra ID > Custom Branding) in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Global Reader is read-only. User Administrator manages users and groups, and Domain Name Administrator manages domain names; neither can change sign-in branding.

prompt: An administrator is adding a custom domain to Microsoft 365 manually. The DNS hosting provider does not allow TXT records to be created. Which alternative can be used to prove ownership of the domain?

options.text: A CNAME record named autodiscover
An MX verification record
An SRV record named _sipfederationtls
A DKIM selector CNAME record

explanation: Domain ownership can be verified with a TXT record or, if TXT records cannot be added, with an MX verification record whose priority is set so that it does not disrupt existing mail. The autodiscover CNAME helps Outlook clients find Exchange Online, the _sipfederationtls SRV record supports Teams federation, and DKIM CNAME records enable message signing; none of them verifies ownership.

prompt: After a divestiture, an administrator tries to remove fabrikam.com from the tenant and the removal is blocked. Several users, a shared mailbox and two Microsoft 365 groups still have addresses in that domain. What must be done first?

options.text: Delete the domain's MX record at the registrar
Add a new onmicrosoft.com domain and make it the fallback domain
Move those users, the mailbox and the groups to another domain
Wait for the domain registration to expire

explanation: A domain can be removed only when it is not the default domain and no users, mailboxes, contacts, groups, distribution lists or teams use it, so those objects must be moved to another domain first. Changing public DNS records or letting the registration lapse does not change what the tenant's objects reference. Adding another onmicrosoft.com fallback domain does not remove dependencies on the custom domain.

prompt: A junior administrator must add, verify and remove custom domains in the Microsoft 365 admin center and should receive no other administrative capability. Which role should be assigned?

options.text: Exchange Administrator
Billing Administrator
Service Support Administrator
Domain Name Administrator

explanation: Domain Name Administrator is the role required to add, modify and remove domains. Exchange Administrator manages mail settings, Billing Administrator manages purchases and subscriptions, and Service Support Administrator works with service health and support requests; none of these is the role for managing domains.

prompt: A domain has been verified in Microsoft 365 and mailboxes use it, but mail sent from the internet still arrives at the company's previous mail host. Which DNS record must be changed to deliver inbound mail to Exchange Online?

options.text: The MX record, so that it points to mail.protection.outlook.com
The SPF TXT record, so that it includes spf.protection.outlook.com
The autodiscover CNAME record, so that it points to autodiscover.outlook.com
The verification TXT record that was used to prove ownership

explanation: Inbound mail routing is determined by the MX record, which must point to the domain's <token>.mail.protection.outlook.com host with the lowest preference value. The SPF TXT record authorizes Microsoft 365 to send mail for the domain. The autodiscover CNAME is used for client configuration, and the verification TXT record only proves ownership.

prompt: A company was renamed from Contoso to Northwind. Its initial domain is contoso.onmicrosoft.com, and management wants the fallback domain to reflect the new name. What can the administrator do?

options.text: Rename contoso.onmicrosoft.com to northwind.onmicrosoft.com
Add a new onmicrosoft.com domain and make it the fallback domain
Delete contoso.onmicrosoft.com and create northwind.onmicrosoft.com in its place
Open a support request to change the tenant ID

explanation: An onmicrosoft.com domain cannot be renamed or removed, but additional onmicrosoft.com domains can be added (up to five in total) and one of them can be made the fallback domain. Renaming and deleting are therefore not possible. Changing the tenant ID is not how a fallback domain is changed; note also that changing the fallback domain does not rename SharePoint URLs.

prompt: A company wants users to be signed out of Microsoft 365 web apps automatically after one hour of inactivity. Where is this configured?

options.text: Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences
Settings > Org settings > Services > Microsoft 365 on the web
Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy > Idle session timeout
Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy > Password expiration policy

explanation: Idle session timeout on the Security & privacy tab of Org settings signs inactive users out of Microsoft 365 web apps across the organization. Release preferences controls how early the organization receives feature updates. The Microsoft 365 on the web service setting does not control inactivity sign-out, and the password expiration policy controls how often passwords must be changed.

prompt: Idle session timeout is turned on for the tenant. The company wants inactive users to be signed out of Microsoft 365 web apps only on unmanaged devices. The tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P1. What else must be configured?

options.text: A sign-in frequency session control of one hour for all users
A device compliance policy that marks unmanaged devices as noncompliant
An authentication strength that requires phishing-resistant MFA
A Conditional Access policy with the 'Use app enforced restrictions' control

explanation: To limit idle session timeout to unmanaged devices, a Conditional Access policy with the 'Use app enforced restrictions' session control is needed in addition to the idle session timeout setting. Sign-in frequency forces periodic reauthentication regardless of activity. A compliance policy only evaluates devices, and an authentication strength governs which methods satisfy sign-in, not inactivity sign-out.

prompt: An auditor requires that passwords of cloud-only users expire every 90 days. The tenant currently uses the default setting. What should a User Administrator change?

options.text: In Password expiration policy, clear the never-expire option and enter 90 days
In Org settings > Security & privacy > Idle session timeout, set the timeout to 90 days
In Microsoft Entra Password Protection, set the lockout duration to 90 days
In the self-service password reset settings, set the reconfirmation period to 90 days

explanation: By default passwords never expire; the Password expiration policy on the Security & privacy tab lets an administrator clear that option and set a period from 14 to 730 days. Idle session timeout controls inactivity sign-out. The smart lockout duration is the time an account stays locked after failed attempts, and the SSPR reconfirmation period controls how often users confirm their registered reset information.

prompt: A company with Microsoft 365 E5 wants Microsoft support engineers to obtain explicit approval from the company before they can access customer content while resolving a support case. What should the administrator turn on?

options.text: Privacy profile
Customer Lockbox
Idle session timeout
Privileged Identity Management

explanation: Customer Lockbox, on the Security & privacy tab of Org settings, requires approval for data access requests from Microsoft engineers. The privacy profile only publishes the organization's privacy statement URL and privacy contact. Idle session timeout signs out inactive users, and Privileged Identity Management governs the company's own administrators' role activations, not access by Microsoft personnel.

prompt: A sales group contains a nested group of contractors. Microsoft 365 E3 licenses were assigned to the sales group in the Microsoft 365 admin center, but the contractors did not receive licenses. Why?

options.text: Contractors must be assigned licenses by a Billing Administrator
Licenses can be assigned only to Microsoft 365 groups, not to security groups
Group-based licensing does not apply licenses to members of nested groups
Group-based licensing applies licenses only after 30 days of membership

explanation: Group-based licensing does not support nested groups; only direct, first-level members of the licensed group receive licenses, so the contractors must be direct members or their group must be licensed itself. License assignment needs a License, User or Groups Administrator rather than a Billing Administrator. Security, mail-enabled and Microsoft 365 groups are all supported, and there is no 30-day waiting period.

prompt: After a licensed group grows, several members show an error on the product's Errors & issues tab because there are not enough licenses. The company buys more licenses. What should the administrator do next so the affected users receive licenses?

options.text: Remove the users from the group and add them again one at a time
Delete the group license assignment and wait 24 hours before re-creating it
Change each affected user's usage location
Select the affected users or group and choose Reprocess

explanation: After the underlying problem is fixed, Reprocess on the Errors & issues tab forces license processing for the affected group or users. Removing and re-adding members or deleting the assignment risks temporary loss of service and is unnecessary. Usage location is unrelated to a shortage of licenses.

prompt: A user is moving from the Sales licensed group to the Marketing licensed group. Both groups assign Microsoft 365 E5. The user must not lose access to services during the change. In which order should the administrator act?

options.text: Add the user to Marketing, confirm the new license, and then remove the user from Sales
Remove the user from Sales, wait for processing, and then add the user to Marketing
Remove the user from both groups and assign the license directly
Disable the user account, change both memberships, and then enable the account

explanation: Adding the user to the destination group first, confirming that the new license assignment is applied, and only then removing the user from the original group avoids a gap in licensing. Removing the user from the source group first leaves the user unlicensed until group-based licensing finishes processing. Direct assignment defeats group-based management, and disabling the account does not prevent a licensing gap.

prompt: An administrator removes the Microsoft 365 license from a user account but does not delete the user. What happens to the user's Exchange Online mailbox data?

options.text: It is deleted immediately and cannot be recovered
It is held for 30 days and then deleted
It is converted automatically to a shared mailbox
It is kept indefinitely until the user account is deleted

explanation: When a license is removed, the user's Exchange Online data is held for 30 days and is then deleted, apart from content protected by retention policies or labels. It is not deleted immediately, and it is not kept indefinitely. Conversion to a shared mailbox is a deliberate administrative action that must be performed while the mailbox is still licensed.

prompt: A billing policy for pay-as-you-go services in the Microsoft 365 admin center has a monthly budget. Spending reaches 100 percent of the budget halfway through the month. What happens?

options.text: The connected services are paused until the next month
The Azure subscription is disabled until an administrator raises the budget
Alert notifications are sent, but the services and billing continue
New usage is automatically charged to a different billing policy

explanation: Budgets on a pay-as-you-go billing policy only generate alerts to the configured email-enabled groups; reaching 100 percent does not stop the service or the billing. Nothing is paused, the Azure subscription is not disabled, and usage is not redirected to another billing policy.

prompt: An administrator tries to assign a Microsoft 365 Copilot license to a user whose only license is Microsoft Entra ID P2, and Copilot does not become available to the user. What is required?

options.text: The user must be added to a role-assignable group
The user must hold the AI Administrator role
The tenant must enable pay-as-you-go billing for Copilot Chat
The user also needs an eligible base license, such as Microsoft 365 E3

explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on that requires an eligible prerequisite plan, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or E5, Business Standard or Office 365 E3; Microsoft Entra ID P2 by itself is not a qualifying plan. Role-assignable groups and the AI Administrator role are about administration rights, not user entitlement. Pay-as-you-go billing covers metered Copilot Chat agent usage, not the Copilot license prerequisite.

prompt: A manager asks how many Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned and how many are still available in the tenant. Where can an administrator see both figures in the Microsoft 365 admin center?

options.text: The Readiness tab of the Copilot usage report
The Service health page under Health
The Network connectivity page under Health
The Restoration tasks tab in Microsoft 365 Backup

explanation: The Readiness tab of the Copilot usage report shows Assigned Licenses and Available Licenses for the tenant. Service health reports incidents and advisories. Network connectivity shows network assessments and insights, and the Restoration tasks tab tracks Microsoft 365 Backup restores.

prompt: A company buys a Copilot Studio prepaid capacity pack. Three makers who will build agents report that they still cannot author in Copilot Studio. They have no Microsoft 365 Copilot license. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Assign the tenant-level Copilot Studio license to each maker
Assign the free Copilot Studio User License to each maker
Assign each maker a Microsoft Agent 365 license
Allocate Copilot Credits to each maker in the Power Platform admin center

explanation: Copilot Studio has a tenant license that carries capacity and cannot be assigned to users, plus a free Copilot Studio User License that is assigned to makers in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Agent 365 is a control plane for governing agents and does not grant authoring rights. Copilot Credits are allocated to environments, not to individual users.

prompt: An administrator must report how many Copilot Credits each Power Platform environment has consumed this month and adjust the capacity allocated to an environment. Where should this be done?

options.text: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses
Microsoft Entra admin center > Billing > Licenses
Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio
Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration

explanation: Copilot Studio capacity is monitored and managed in the Power Platform admin center under Licensing > Copilot Studio, which has summary and environment views, downloadable reports and capacity management. The Microsoft 365 admin center Licenses page shows license counts and assignments, not credit consumption per environment. The Entra admin center no longer manages license assignment in its interface, and the Defender portal is unrelated to capacity.

prompt: A production environment's agents were blocked with a usage-limit message after consumption significantly exceeded the tenant's prepaid Copilot Credits. The business wants agents in this environment to keep working during future spikes and accepts metered charges. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Assign the Copilot Studio User License to every agent end user
Assign Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses to the makers of the agents
Set a lower per-agent monthly limit with a hard stop
Bill the environment's overage to a pay-as-you-go plan

explanation: Environments whose overage is billed to a pay-as-you-go plan are not blocked when prepaid capacity is exceeded, whereas enforcement otherwise blocks agents once usage passes 125 percent of prepaid capacity. End users of agents do not need a license, so assigning user licenses changes nothing. Licensing the makers does not cover usage by other users, and a lower hard-stop limit would block agents sooner.

prompt: A company with Microsoft 365 E5 wants premium Microsoft Agent 365 capabilities for governing agents, such as Conditional Access for agents. How is Agent 365 licensed?

options.text: Per user, as a stand-alone subscription or as part of Microsoft 365 E7
Per tenant, as a free feature of every Microsoft Entra ID P1 tenant
Per message, through Copilot Credits bought in capacity packs
Per device, through a Microsoft Intune add-on

explanation: Microsoft Agent 365 is licensed per user and is available as a stand-alone subscription for eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions or included in Microsoft 365 E7. It is not a free part of Microsoft Entra ID P1. Copilot Credits are the consumption currency for Copilot Studio, not the Agent 365 license, and Agent 365 is not licensed per device through Intune.

prompt: A company wants to start protecting SharePoint sites and Exchange mailboxes with Microsoft 365 Backup. No setup has been done. What must be in place before backup policies can be created?

options.text: A Microsoft 365 E5 license for every protected user
Pay-as-you-go billing linked to an Azure subscription
A Recovery Services vault in Azure Backup
A Microsoft Purview retention policy for each workload

explanation: Microsoft 365 Backup is a consumption-based, pay-as-you-go service, so billing must be set up with an Azure subscription (with a resource group and region) before policies are created under Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup. It is not licensed per user through E5. Azure Backup vaults protect Azure resources, not Microsoft 365 data, and Purview retention policies are separate and do not affect the backup recovery window.

prompt: Ransomware encrypted the content of 300 SharePoint sites that are protected by Microsoft 365 Backup. The business needs the sites back in a healthy state as fast as possible. Which restore choice gives the fastest recovery?

options.text: Restore to new URLs by using the most recent standard restore point
Restore each file individually by using granular file restore
Replace the sites in place from an express restore point
Remove the sites from the policy and add them again before restoring

explanation: For full SharePoint site and OneDrive account restores, the fastest recovery comes from an in-place (same URL) restore that uses one of the recommended express restore points. Restores to new URLs and from standard restore points are slower. Granular file restore is meant for a few files, and removing the sites from the policy does nothing to speed up a restore.

prompt: A site owner suspects that a SharePoint site was damaged last week. Before anything is overwritten, the administrator wants to examine the backed-up version of the site alongside the current site. Which restore destination should be chosen in Microsoft 365 Backup?

options.text: Replace sites with backups
Restore to the site collection recycle bin
Restore to the owner's OneDrive
Create new sites from backups

explanation: 'Create new sites from backups' restores to a new URL, leaving the current site untouched so the two can be compared. 'Replace sites with backups' rolls the existing site back and overwrites content, metadata and permissions changed since the restore point. Microsoft 365 Backup does not restore sites into a recycle bin or into a user's OneDrive.

prompt: An administrator removes a OneDrive account from the scope of a Microsoft 365 Backup policy. What happens to that account's backups?

options.text: No new backups are taken, but existing backups are kept and still charged
All existing backups are deleted immediately and charges stop
Backups continue until the policy itself is paused
Existing backups are exported to the tenant's Azure storage account

explanation: A removed item moves to the Removed Items tab: no further backups are taken, but the backups already taken are preserved for the recovery window that applied and are still billed. They are not deleted immediately; deleting them is a separate action with a grace period. Backups do not continue after removal, and data is not exported to Azure storage.

prompt: One administrator must manage Microsoft 365 Backup policies and restores for OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange. The Global Administrator role must not be used. Which single role should be assigned?

options.text: SharePoint Administrator
Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator
Exchange Administrator
Billing Administrator

explanation: The Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator role can manage backup for OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange. SharePoint Administrator covers only OneDrive and SharePoint backups, and Exchange Administrator covers only Exchange backups. Billing Administrator manages purchases and billing, not backup policies or restores.

prompt: During a large Microsoft 365 Backup restore of several hundred mailboxes, an administrator needs to follow the progress of the restore jobs. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: The Issue history tab in Service health
Cost Management in the Azure portal
The Restoration tasks tab in Microsoft 365 Backup
Message trace in the Exchange admin center

explanation: Restore progress is tracked on the Restoration tasks tab of Microsoft 365 Backup. Issue history in Service health lists resolved service incidents and advisories. Azure Cost Management shows what the service costs, and message trace follows the delivery of individual email messages.

prompt: A company has three offices in the same city. On the Network connectivity page of the Microsoft 365 admin center, their measurements are merged into a single city-level location. How can the administrator get a separate network assessment for each office?

options.text: Turn on Windows Location Services on more computers in each office
Create a separate Microsoft Entra named location for each office
Create a separate billing policy for each office
Add each office as a location with its LAN subnet information

explanation: Adding office locations with their LAN subnets lets network connectivity attribute measurements to individual offices, including several offices in one city. Windows Location Services resolves locations only to city level. Microsoft Entra named locations are used by Conditional Access and are not read by the network connectivity page, and billing policies relate to pay-as-you-go services.

prompt: A branch office with a single Windows computer needs a quick, one-time check of its network path to Microsoft 365, with the results visible in the admin center within minutes. What should be used?

options.text: The Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool
Windows Location Services, enabled on that computer
A message trace run from the Exchange admin center
The Microsoft 365 Apps usage report

explanation: The Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool can be run on a Windows computer while signed in to the tenant and its results appear in the admin center within a few minutes. Collection through Windows Location Services needs at least two computers at the office location and takes about a day to show data. Message trace follows email delivery, and usage reports show activity rather than network quality.

prompt: A small office is expected to appear on the Network connectivity page through Windows Location Services. Its only Windows computer has location turned on, runs an up-to-date OneDrive sync app and is connected through Wi-Fi, but the office never appears. Which requirement is not met?

options.text: The computer must use a wired Ethernet connection
At least two computers at the location must report
The office must have at least 500 users
The computer must be signed in with a Network Administrator account

explanation: Detection through Windows Location Services needs at least two computers at an office location running the OneDrive sync app with location enabled on Wi-Fi. Wired Ethernet is not what this method relies on. There is no 500-user minimum for a location to appear, and the end-user computers do not need an administrator signed in.

prompt: The Network connectivity page shows the insight 'User connections to Microsoft 365 domains are being TLS intercepted and decrypted by a network intermediary'. Which change is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Raise the idle session timeout for Microsoft 365 web apps
Add the office's egress IP address as a trusted named location
Configure the proxy to bypass TLS inspection for Microsoft 365 traffic
Move the affected users to Targeted release

explanation: The insight reports that a proxy or other intermediary is decrypting Microsoft 365 traffic, so the remedy is to exclude Microsoft 365 traffic from TLS inspection on that device. Idle session timeout and release preferences are unrelated to the network path. A trusted named location affects Conditional Access decisions and does not stop a device from intercepting traffic.

prompt: An administrator wants to be emailed whenever Microsoft posts an incident that affects Exchange Online or Microsoft Teams. Where is this configured?

options.text: Message center > Preferences > Custom view
Org settings > Security & privacy > Privacy profile
Billing > Billing notifications
Service health > Customize > Email

explanation: On the Service health page, Customize > Email lets an administrator turn on email notifications for incidents and/or advisories, choose the services, and specify up to two email addresses. Message center preferences concern announcements about planned changes. The privacy profile holds the organization's privacy contact, and billing notifications are about invoices.

prompt: A change manager needs advance notice of planned maintenance and upcoming feature changes for Microsoft 365. Where should the change manager look?

options.text: Message center
The Issue history tab in Service health
The Reported issues tab in Service health
The Network connectivity page

explanation: Planned maintenance and upcoming changes are announced in Message center; they are not shown in Service health. Issue history lists resolved incidents and advisories from the last 7 or 30 days. Reported issues tracks problems the organization itself reported, and Network connectivity shows network assessments and insights.

prompt: During a widespread outage, administrators cannot sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center. Where can they check the current status of Microsoft 365 services?

options.text: The Microsoft Entra admin center sign-in logs
The service status page at status.cloud.microsoft
The Microsoft Defender portal Action center
The SharePoint admin center Active sites page

explanation: When the admin center cannot be reached, Microsoft publishes service status on the public status page at status.cloud.microsoft. The Entra sign-in logs, the Defender Action center and the SharePoint admin center all require a successful sign-in and do not report Microsoft 365 service incidents.

prompt: Several users cannot open files in OneDrive, but the Service health page lists no active incident or advisory for OneDrive. The administrator wants Microsoft to check whether there is a service problem. What should the administrator do on the Service health page?

options.text: Select Customize and add OneDrive to the custom view
Open Issue history and reopen the most recent OneDrive incident
Select Report an issue and complete the form
Open the Reported issues tab and wait for an entry to appear

explanation: Report an issue lets an administrator submit a short form; if Microsoft confirms the problem, it is added as an incident or advisory, and the report can be tracked on the Reported issues tab. A custom view only filters which services are displayed. Past issues cannot be reopened from Issue history, and the Reported issues tab only lists what has already been reported.

prompt: On the Service health page, a SharePoint item is described as affecting some users while the service remains available and a workaround exists. How is this item classified?

options.text: Incident
Plan for change
Issue for your organization to act on
Advisory

explanation: An advisory describes a problem that affects some users while the service is still available, often with a workaround or limited scope. An incident is a critical issue in which a service or major function is unavailable. 'Plan for change' is a Message center category, and 'Issues for your organization to act on' lists problems in the organization's own environment that need the organization's action.

prompt: The shared mailbox info@contoso.com has no license assigned and has reached 50 GB. Users report that they can no longer send messages from it. The mailbox must keep all of its existing content and continue to grow. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Assign an Exchange Online Plan 2 license to the shared mailbox
Grant the affected users the Send As permission again
Convert the shared mailbox to a Microsoft 365 group
Enable sign-in for the shared mailbox account

explanation: An unlicensed shared mailbox can store up to 50 GB; assigning an Exchange Online Plan 2 license raises the limit to 100 GB. Granting Send As again does not help because the problem is the storage limit, not permissions. Converting to a Microsoft 365 group is not a supported way to keep the mailbox and its content, and enabling sign-in for the shared mailbox account has no effect on its quota and weakens security.

prompt: Members of the reception team have Full Access to the shared mailbox reception@fabrikam.com. Replies must look as if they came from the reception address itself, with no indication of which person sent them. Which permission should the administrator add?

options.text: Send on Behalf
Send As
Read and manage
Reviewer on the Sent Items folder

explanation: Send As makes a message appear to come from the shared mailbox itself. Send on Behalf would show the sender as, for example, 'Dana on behalf of Reception', which reveals the individual. Read and manage is the Full Access permission the team already has and does not allow sending, and a Reviewer folder permission only lets someone read a folder.

prompt: A user who left the company had a licensed 20 GB mailbox that the sales team must keep monitoring. The company wants to free the license while keeping the mailbox available to the team. What should the administrator do first?

options.text: Delete the user account and restore the mailbox as an inactive mailbox
Remove the license and then add the team as delegates
Export the mailbox to a PST file and import it to a Microsoft 365 group
Convert the mailbox to a shared mailbox, then remove the license

explanation: A user mailbox must still be licensed when it is converted to a shared mailbox; after the conversion the license can be removed because the mailbox is under 50 GB. Deleting the user account removes the account that anchors the mailbox, and an inactive mailbox is not available for a team to work in. Removing the license first would disconnect the mailbox before it could be converted, and a PST export to a group is unnecessary manual work that loses the mailbox address and structure.

prompt: Agents send mail from a shared support mailbox by using the Send As permission. Other agents cannot see what was sent because each message is stored only in the sending agent's own Sent Items folder. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Enable an archive mailbox for the shared mailbox
Grant each agent the Send on Behalf permission instead
Run Set-Mailbox with -MessageCopyForSentAsEnabled $true
Create a mail flow rule that adds the shared mailbox as a Bcc recipient

explanation: By default a message sent as a shared mailbox is saved in the sender's own Sent Items; setting MessageCopyForSentAsEnabled to $true on the shared mailbox also saves a copy in the shared mailbox's Sent Items. An archive mailbox only adds storage. Switching to Send on Behalf changes how the sender is displayed and has its own separate copy setting, and a Bcc mail flow rule would deliver copies to the Inbox rather than Sent Items.

prompt: An administrator grants Full Access to a shared mailbox to a mail-enabled security group. Group members can open the mailbox manually, but it does not appear automatically in Outlook as it does for users who were granted access individually. Why?

options.text: Automapping does not work when Full Access is granted through a group
Automapping requires the shared mailbox to have an Exchange Online license
Automapping is disabled by default and must be enabled per tenant
Automapping requires the Send As permission in addition to Full Access

explanation: Automapping is on by default but is recorded against the individual user's mailbox, so it does not work when access comes from a security group. A shared mailbox under 50 GB needs no license for automapping. It is not a tenant-level feature that is off by default, and Send As controls sending, not whether the mailbox is added to Outlook.

prompt: After a user mailbox is converted to a shared mailbox, a security review finds that the former employee's password still allows interactive sign-in to the account. The mailbox must remain available to its delegates. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Delete the user account that is associated with the shared mailbox
Remove the Exchange Online license from the account
Remove the Full Access permission from all delegates
Block sign-in for the shared mailbox's associated account

explanation: A converted mailbox keeps its original password until it is reset, so sign-in should be blocked for the associated account; delegates use their own credentials and are unaffected. Deleting the account would delete the shared mailbox because the account anchors it. Removing the license does not stop authentication, and removing Full Access from delegates would stop the people who should be using the mailbox.

prompt: A shared mailbox that holds 12 GB of mail must be placed on litigation hold for a legal case. The hold option cannot be applied. What is required?

options.text: Convert the shared mailbox back to a user mailbox permanently
Assign the mailbox an Exchange Online Plan 2 license
Grant the compliance officer Full Access to the shared mailbox
Increase the mailbox quota by enabling auto-expanding archiving

explanation: Although a shared mailbox under 50 GB needs no license for normal use, litigation hold and archiving require Exchange Online Plan 2, or Exchange Online Plan 1 plus Exchange Online Archiving. Converting the mailbox to a user mailbox is not needed. Full Access for a compliance officer is a permission, not a hold, and auto-expanding archiving is itself a licensed feature that does not place content on hold.

prompt: A Microsoft Teams team was deleted by its owner 12 days ago. The team's channels, files and membership must be recovered. What should a Teams administrator do?

options.text: Restore the team's site from Deleted sites in the SharePoint admin center only
Create a new team from the same team template
Restore the team from the deleted teams view in the Teams admin center
Run a content search and export the channel messages to a new team

explanation: A deleted team is soft-deleted with its Microsoft 365 group for 30 days and can be restored from Manage teams > View deleted teams in the Teams admin center, which restores the group and its resources. Restoring only the SharePoint site does not bring back the team, channels or membership. A template creates an empty team, and a content search export cannot rebuild a working team.

prompt: A project has finished. Its team must stay visible for reference, but nobody should be able to post in channels or change the files in the team's document library. Which action meets the requirement?

options.text: Archive the team and make the SharePoint site read-only for members
Delete the team and rely on the 30-day soft-delete period
Demote every owner to member
Change the team's privacy from public to private

explanation: Archiving makes the team's conversations read-only, and the optional setting makes the connected SharePoint site read-only for team members so files cannot be edited either. Deleting removes the team from view and it is permanently lost after 30 days. Demoting owners still lets members post and edit, and changing privacy only affects who can find and join the team.

prompt: A team must collaborate in one channel with employees of a partner organization. The partner's users must not be added to the team or created as guest accounts, and they should stay signed in to their own tenant. What should be used?

options.text: A standard channel with guest access enabled
A private channel
A separate team with the partner users added as guests
A shared channel

explanation: Shared channels let people outside the team, including external users through Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect, take part without guest accounts and without switching tenants. A standard channel is open to the whole team and external people would need to be guests of the team. A private channel is limited to a subset of existing team members, and a separate team with guests violates the no-guest-account requirement.

prompt: Five members of a 200-person team, one of whom is a guest in the tenant, need a confidential space inside the team with its own separate file storage. Which channel type should the team owner create?

options.text: A shared channel
A private channel
A standard channel with channel moderation turned on
A standard channel in a hidden state

explanation: A private channel is restricted to a subset of the team's members, supports guests who are already team members, and gets its own SharePoint site. Shared channels do not support guest accounts. Moderation only controls who can start posts, and hiding a standard channel just removes it from a user's own channel list; in both cases all team members keep access.

prompt: A company wants to stop users in the contractors group from creating private channels while leaving all other users unchanged. What should the Teams administrator do?

options.text: Create a meeting policy that disables private meetings and assign it to the group
Create a messaging policy that disables chat and assign it to the group
Create a teams policy with private channel creation off and assign it
Create an app setup policy that unpins the Teams app and assign it to the group

explanation: Teams policies (Teams > Teams policies) contain the Create private channels and Create shared channels settings and can be assigned to users or groups. Meeting policies govern meeting features, messaging policies govern chat and channel messaging features, and app setup policies control pinned and installed apps; none of them controls channel creation.

prompt: The membership of the Sales team must always match the users whose department attribute is Sales, with no manual maintenance by team owners. The tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Change the team's Microsoft 365 group to dynamic membership with a rule
Add a security group that contains the sales users as a member of the team
Convert the team to an org-wide team
Create a team template that lists the sales users

explanation: A team backed by a Microsoft 365 group with a dynamic membership rule (which requires Microsoft Entra ID P1) is kept in step with user attributes, and owners can no longer add or remove members manually. Adding a security group to a team only copies its current members once and does not stay synchronized. An org-wide team includes everyone in the organization, and team templates do not include membership.

prompt: A team member tries to add a shared channel and the option is unavailable. The teams policy assigned to the user allows the creation of shared channels. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Shared channels can be created only in public teams
Shared channels require the user to hold the Teams Administrator role
The team has reached the limit of 30 shared channels
Only team owners can create shared channels

explanation: Members can create standard and, if allowed, private channels, but only team owners can create shared channels, in addition to the teams policy allowing it. Shared channels are not limited to public teams and do not need an admin role. Channels of all types count toward the overall per-team channel limit of 1,000 rather than a limit of 30 shared channels.

prompt: Compliance requires that Microsoft 365 Copilot is used in Teams meetings only when a transcript is saved, and meeting organizers must not be able to choose a different Copilot behavior. Which value should be set for Copilot in the meeting policy?

options.text: On
On with saved transcript required
On with transcript saved by default
Off

explanation: 'On with saved transcript required' sets the organizer's option to 'During and after the meeting' and enforces it so organizers cannot change it. 'On' defaults organizers to 'Only during the meeting' and lets them change it. 'On with transcript saved by default' uses the same default as the correct answer but organizers can change it, and 'Off' defaults Copilot to off for the meeting.

prompt: A legal department wants its organizers' meetings to default to Copilot being available only while the meeting is running, with nothing kept afterward, while still letting an organizer pick another option for a specific meeting. Which Copilot value should the meeting policy assigned to those users have?

options.text: On with transcript saved by default
Off
On
On with saved transcript required

explanation: With the policy value 'On', the organizer's meeting option defaults to 'Only during the meeting' and the organizer can still change it. 'On with transcript saved by default' and 'On with saved transcript required' both default to 'During and after the meeting', and the latter cannot be changed. 'Off' sets the default to no Copilot in the meeting.

prompt: After a meeting in which the Copilot meeting option was 'Only during the meeting', a licensed participant asks why Copilot cannot answer questions about the meeting from the meeting chat the next day. What is the explanation?

options.text: Copilot used temporary speech-to-text data that is not kept
The participant needs the Teams Premium license to query past meetings
The organizer must first publish the recap from the Recap tab
Meeting data becomes available to Copilot only after 24 hours of indexing

explanation: With 'Only during the meeting', Copilot works from temporary speech-to-text data that is not kept once the meeting ends, so there is nothing to query afterward; 'During and after the meeting' with a transcript is needed for that. A Microsoft 365 Copilot license, not Teams Premium, is what the feature needs. There is no publish step for a recap that unlocks Copilot, and the limitation is not caused by an indexing delay.

prompt: Organizers' meetings use the Copilot option 'During and after the meeting', but Copilot cannot be used unless another participant happens to start transcription. The organizers cannot start transcription themselves. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Turn on Transcription in the organizers' meeting policy
Turn on cloud recording expiration in the meeting policy
Assign the organizers a Teams policy that allows shared channels
Set the live captions setting to Off in the meeting policy

explanation: 'During and after the meeting' needs a transcript to be started; if the organizer's meeting policy has Transcription off, Copilot is unusable unless another permitted participant starts it. Recording expiration only controls how long recordings are kept. A teams policy for shared channels is unrelated to meetings, and turning live captions off does not allow transcription.

prompt: A meeting organizer sets the Copilot meeting option to Off for a confidential meeting. What else does this choice do for that meeting?

options.text: It removes the meeting chat for external participants
It prevents participants from sharing their screens
It applies end-to-end encryption to the meeting
It turns off recording and transcription for the meeting

explanation: When the organizer sets the Copilot option to Off, recording and transcription are also disabled for that meeting. The option does not remove chat or restrict screen sharing, which are controlled by other meeting options and policies. End-to-end encryption is a separate setting, and Copilot is in fact unavailable in end-to-end encrypted meetings.

prompt: An administrator scripts Teams configuration and needs the executives' meeting policy to default Copilot to 'During and after the meeting' while still letting organizers change the option. Which command should be used?

options.text: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Executives -Copilot Enabled
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Executives -Copilot EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Executives -Copilot EnabledWithTranscript
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Executives -Copilot Disabled

explanation: EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn corresponds to 'On with transcript saved by default': the default is 'During and after the meeting' and organizers may change it. Enabled defaults to 'Only during the meeting'. EnabledWithTranscript enforces 'During and after the meeting' so organizers cannot change it, and Disabled defaults Copilot to off.

prompt: A communication site was deleted from the SharePoint admin center 60 days ago and is now needed again. What should the SharePoint administrator do?

options.text: Open a support request, because sites are recoverable by administrators for only 30 days
Restore the site from the site collection recycle bin of the root site
Restore the site from the Deleted sites page in the SharePoint admin center
Create a new site with the same URL and restore the files from version history

explanation: Deleted sites are retained for 93 days and can be restored from Deleted sites in the SharePoint admin center. The 30-day figure applies to the other resources of a deleted Microsoft 365 group, not to the site itself. The root site's recycle bin holds deleted items and subsites, not other site collections, and a new site has no version history of the old content.

prompt: The organization-level sharing setting for SharePoint is 'New and existing guests'. The owner of a marketing site asks for the site to allow 'Anyone' links. What must happen for this to be possible?

options.text: The site owner must be made a site admin
The site must be converted to a communication site
The site must be associated with a hub that allows Anyone links
The organization-level setting must first be changed to Anyone

explanation: A site's external sharing setting can be the same as or more restrictive than the organization-level setting, never more permissive, so the organization-level setting must be raised to Anyone first. Being a site admin does not override the tenant limit. The site type and hub association do not determine the maximum sharing level.

prompt: Members of the finance department must be able to open and read documents on a SharePoint team site but must not be able to add or change content. Following the default SharePoint groups, where should the administrator add them?

options.text: The site Visitors group
The site Members group
The site Owners group
The site admins list

explanation: The default Visitors group has the Read permission level. The Members group has Edit, which allows adding and changing content, the Owners group has Full Control, and site admins also have full control of the whole site.

prompt: During an investigation, all access to a specific SharePoint site (not the root site) must be blocked temporarily without deleting the site or changing its permissions. What should the SharePoint administrator do?

options.text: Set the site's external sharing to 'Only people in your organization'
Run Set-SPOSite for the site with -LockState NoAccess
Remove the site from its hub in the SharePoint admin center
Archive the Microsoft Teams team that is connected to the site

explanation: Setting the lock state to NoAccess with Set-SPOSite blocks everyone from the site until it is unlocked, leaving content and permissions intact. Restricting external sharing only affects guests and links. Removing a hub association changes navigation and branding only, and archiving a team makes content read-only at most rather than blocking access.

prompt: To reclaim storage, an administrator plans to delete the SharePoint site that belongs to a Microsoft 365 group-connected team. The team still uses its channels every day. What should the administrator know before proceeding?

options.text: Only the files are removed; the team and its conversations keep working
The site is moved to the owner's OneDrive and can be reattached later
The Microsoft 365 group, its mailbox and the team are deleted too
The site cannot be deleted until every channel has been archived

explanation: Deleting a group-connected site deletes the Microsoft 365 group and its resources, such as the group mailbox and the Teams team. The team therefore does not keep working, nothing is moved to OneDrive, and there is no requirement to archive channels first.

prompt: A human resources site is found to be overshared. While permissions are being cleaned up, the site's content must not surface in Microsoft 365 Copilot or organization-wide search, but people who already have access must still be able to open the site and search within it. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A NoAccess lock on the site
Restricted access control for the site
Restricted content discovery for the site
A block download policy for the site

explanation: Restricted content discovery hides a site's content from organization-wide search and Copilot without changing permissions, and searching inside the site keeps working. A NoAccess lock blocks everyone. Restricted access control changes who can open the site by limiting it to specified groups, and a block download policy only prevents downloading, printing and syncing.

prompt: Files on a research site have been shared individually with many employees over time. The company now requires that only members of the Research security group can open anything on the site, even if a file was shared with someone else. Which SharePoint Advanced Management feature should be used?

options.text: Restricted access control
Restricted content discovery
Site access review
Inactive site policy

explanation: Restricted access control limits access to members of the specified Microsoft 365 or security groups who also have permissions, so other users are denied even when a file was shared with them. Restricted content discovery only hides content from organization-wide search and Copilot and does not change who can open it. A site access review asks owners to review access but enforces nothing by itself, and an inactive site policy deals with unused sites.

prompt: Before a Copilot rollout, an administrator needs a list of sites where content is shared with 'Everyone except external users' and sites with large numbers of sharing links. Where should the administrator look?

options.text: The usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The Service health page in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The Active sites storage column in the SharePoint admin center
The data access governance reports

explanation: Data access governance reports in SharePoint Advanced Management include sharing links reports and 'Everyone except external users' insights that identify potentially overshared sites. Microsoft 365 usage reports show activity and storage, not sharing exposure. Service health shows service incidents, and the storage column only shows how much space a site uses.

prompt: A company has assigned Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses to 300 users. The SharePoint administrator wants to use SharePoint Advanced Management features such as data access governance reports and restricted content discovery. What licensing action is needed?

options.text: Buy a SharePoint Advanced Management add-on license for every SharePoint user
None; the features are available because users have Copilot licenses
Upgrade every user to Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance
Enable pay-as-you-go billing for SharePoint in the Microsoft 365 admin center

explanation: SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities become available when at least one user in the organization has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, so no additional purchase is needed for these features. A per-user add-on is the alternative for organizations without Copilot licenses. E5 Compliance does not provide SharePoint Advanced Management, and pay-as-you-go billing is used for other services such as Microsoft 365 Backup.

prompt: A document library holds superseded drafts. Its items must not appear in any search results, including searches run inside the site itself, while the rest of the site stays searchable. What should be configured?

options.text: Restricted content discovery for the site
Set 'Allow this site to appear in Search results' to No in the site settings
A site access review for the site
Set 'Allow items from this document library to appear in search results' to No

explanation: The library-level advanced setting removes that library's items from the search index, so they stop appearing in both organization-wide and site searches while the rest of the site is unaffected. Restricted content discovery applies to the whole site and leaves site-scoped search working. The site-level search setting would remove the entire site from results, and a site access review does not affect search.

prompt: A user account was deleted by mistake 20 days ago. The user needs the same account back, including its group memberships and licenses. What should a User Administrator do?

options.text: Restore the user from Deleted users in the Microsoft Entra admin center
Create a new user with the same user principal name
Open a support request, because deleted users are recoverable for only 14 days
Restore the user's mailbox from Microsoft 365 Backup

explanation: Deleted users are kept for 30 days and can be restored from Users > Deleted users, which brings back the same object and its license assignments. A new account with the same name is a different object with a new ID and none of the old access. The retention period is 30 days, not 14, and Microsoft 365 Backup restores mailbox or site content rather than directory accounts.

prompt: A user reports that a laptop with an active Microsoft 365 session was stolen. The administrator has already disabled the account. Which additional action invalidates the user's refresh tokens so that existing sessions must reauthenticate?

options.text: Remove the user's licenses
Run Revoke-MgUserSignInSession for the user
Change the user's usage location
Remove the user from all groups and teams

explanation: Revoke-MgUserSignInSession (or Revoke sessions in the admin center) invalidates the user's refresh tokens, so apps must sign in again, which fails because the account is disabled. Removing licenses or group memberships changes entitlements but does not invalidate tokens, and usage location only affects license assignment.

prompt: First-line support staff must reset passwords for ordinary users who hold no administrator roles. They must not be able to reset the passwords of Helpdesk Administrators or other administrators. Which role is the least privileged that meets the requirement?

options.text: User Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Password Administrator
Privileged Authentication Administrator

explanation: Password Administrator can reset passwords for non-administrators and only a very small set of roles such as other Password Administrators. Helpdesk Administrator can additionally reset passwords of other Helpdesk Administrators and some reader roles. User Administrator can also reset passwords of several administrator roles and manage users, and Privileged Authentication Administrator can reset any user's password, including Global Administrators.

prompt: A Global Administrator is locked out after forgetting the password. The company wants a delegated role, other than Global Administrator, that is able to reset this administrator's password. Which role can do this?

options.text: Helpdesk Administrator
User Administrator
Authentication Administrator
Privileged Authentication Administrator

explanation: Only Privileged Authentication Administrator and Global Administrator can reset passwords and manage authentication methods for all users, including Global Administrators. Helpdesk Administrator, User Administrator and Authentication Administrator are limited to non-administrators and a defined subset of lower-privileged roles.

prompt: A script that assigns Microsoft 365 licenses to newly synchronized users fails for every account. The accounts were synchronized from on-premises Active Directory with default settings. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The UsageLocation property is not set on the accounts
The accounts are not members of a role-assignable group
The accounts have not registered for multifactor authentication
The accounts are missing the MailNickname property

explanation: A license can be assigned only when the user has a valid UsageLocation, and synchronized accounts do not have one by default; it can be set with Update-MgUser -UsageLocation. Role-assignable groups are for assigning Microsoft Entra roles. MFA registration is not a prerequisite for licensing, and synchronized users already have a mail nickname.

prompt: A company wants only User Administrators and a few project coordinators to be able to invite guest users. Ordinary members and existing guests must not be able to invite anyone. Which configuration meets the requirement?

options.text: Set Guest user access to the most restrictive option and assign the coordinators the Directory Readers role
Set Guest invite settings to 'Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users' and assign the coordinators the Guest Inviter role
Set Guest invite settings to 'No one in the organization can invite guest users' and assign the coordinators the Guest Inviter role
Block B2B collaboration in the default cross-tenant access settings

explanation: With 'Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users', invitations are limited to roles such as User Administrator and Guest Inviter, so assigning Guest Inviter to the coordinators delegates exactly that ability. Guest user access controls what guests can see in the directory, not who can invite. The 'No one' option stops all invitations, and blocking B2B collaboration would stop guest collaboration altogether.

prompt: Employees must be prevented from sending B2B invitations to users in the domain competitor.com, while invitations to all other domains stay allowed. What should the administrator configure in External collaboration settings?

options.text: Guest user access set to the most restrictive option
External user leave settings
Collaboration restrictions that deny the specified domain
An inbound trust setting for multifactor authentication

explanation: Collaboration restrictions can deny invitations to listed domains while allowing all others. Guest user access controls what guests can read in the directory after they are added. External user leave settings control whether external users can remove themselves, and inbound trust settings are part of cross-tenant access settings and deal with accepting MFA and device claims.

prompt: Contoso and Fabrikam want their employees to work together in Teams shared channels without guest accounts being created. Both companies have Microsoft Entra ID P1. What must be configured?

options.text: Teams external access for the other company's domain, in one tenant only
Email one-time passcode as the first identity provider in the redemption order
A dynamic membership group for the other company's users in each tenant
B2B direct connect in cross-tenant access settings, in both tenants

explanation: Shared channels with another organization use Microsoft Entra B2B direct connect, which is blocked by default and must be enabled through cross-tenant access settings in both tenants. Teams external access only allows finding, calling and chatting. The redemption order applies to B2B collaboration guest invitations, and dynamic groups cannot contain users who have no account in the tenant.

prompt: Guests from a partner tenant already complete multifactor authentication in their home tenant. When they open the company's resources, a Conditional Access policy makes them register and perform MFA again in the company's tenant. How can the second prompt be avoided while still requiring MFA?

options.text: Configure inbound trust settings to trust MFA from the partner tenant
Exclude all guest users from the Conditional Access policy
Set Guest user access to 'same access as members'
Enable B2B direct connect outbound access for the partner

explanation: Inbound trust settings in cross-tenant access settings let the resource tenant accept MFA claims from the partner's tenant, so the policy is satisfied by the MFA already performed there. Excluding guests would remove the MFA requirement entirely. Guest user access controls directory visibility, and outbound B2B direct connect governs the company's own users accessing the partner, not partner users coming in.

prompt: A security review finds that guest users can enumerate the members of groups in the directory. The company wants guests to be able to read only their own profile and nothing about other directory objects. Which setting should be changed?

options.text: Guest invite settings, to 'No one in the organization can invite guest users'
Guest user access, to 'restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects'
Collaboration restrictions, to allow only specified domains
The UserType of each guest, to Member

explanation: The most restrictive Guest user access option limits guests to the properties and memberships of their own directory objects. Guest invite settings and collaboration restrictions control who can be invited and from which domains, not what guests can read. Changing UserType to Member would give guests the broader default permissions of members.

prompt: Sales staff need to find, call and chat in Teams with people at a supplier who use their own organization's Teams accounts. The supplier's users must not get accounts in the company's tenant or access to teams and files. Which feature should be used?

options.text: Guest access
A shared channel
External access
A Microsoft 365 group with external members

explanation: Teams external access lets users find, call and chat with people in other organizations without those people having an account in the tenant or access to teams and their files. Guest access creates a Microsoft Entra B2B guest account and gives access to team resources. A shared channel gives external participants access to channel content, and adding external members to a Microsoft 365 group makes them guests.

prompt: The owner of a Microsoft 365 group cannot add a new colleague because the options to add or remove members are unavailable. Other owners manage members of their groups without problems. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The group has reached the maximum of 100 owners
The group is a role-assignable group
The group has expired and must be renewed
The group uses dynamic membership based on a rule

explanation: Members of a dynamic membership group are calculated from a rule and cannot be added or removed manually; the colleague is added when their attributes match the rule. Having many owners does not disable member management. A role-assignable group uses assigned membership that owners can manage, and an expired group is deleted rather than left with disabled controls.

prompt: Hundreds of Microsoft 365 groups are no longer used. The company wants groups to be deleted automatically unless they are renewed, with owners notified before deletion. The tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P1. What should be configured?

options.text: A group expiration policy
A group naming policy
An inactive site policy in SharePoint Advanced Management
A retention policy for Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Purview

explanation: A group expiration policy applies a lifetime to Microsoft 365 groups; owners are notified 30, 15 and 1 day before expiry, groups with activity are renewed automatically, and expired groups are deleted and remain restorable for 30 days. A naming policy only controls group names. An inactive site policy notifies site owners but does not expire groups, and a retention policy preserves or deletes content rather than removing unused groups.

prompt: A company wants every Microsoft 365 group created by users to start with the creator's department and wants names that contain words such as 'Payroll' or 'CEO' to be rejected. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A dynamic membership rule that uses user.department
A group naming policy with a prefix and blocked words
A sensitivity label with the Groups & sites scope
A group expiration policy for selected groups

explanation: The Microsoft 365 groups naming policy supports prefixes and suffixes based on fixed strings or attributes such as [Department], together with a custom blocked words list. A dynamic membership rule decides who is a member, not what the group is called. Sensitivity labels control privacy and guest access settings, and an expiration policy controls group lifetime.

prompt: A Microsoft 365 group that backs a project team was deleted 10 days ago. The group's mailbox, site and membership are needed again. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a new group with the same name and email address
Restore the SharePoint site and then connect it to a new group
Restore the group from Deleted groups
Restore the group mailbox from an inactive mailbox

explanation: A deleted Microsoft 365 group is soft-deleted for 30 days and can be restored from Deleted groups, which also restores its associated resources and membership. A new group with the same name is a different object with empty resources. Restoring only the site does not bring back the mailbox or members, and inactive mailboxes relate to deleted user mailboxes under a hold.

prompt: An administrator tries to assign the Exchange Administrator role to an existing security group named Mail-Admins, but the group cannot be selected. What is required?

options.text: The group must be converted to a Microsoft 365 group
The group must use dynamic membership
The existing group's isAssignableToRole property must be changed to true
A new group must be created as assignable to Microsoft Entra roles

explanation: Only role-assignable groups can be assigned Microsoft Entra roles, and the isAssignableToRole property can be set only when the group is created; it cannot be changed afterward. The group type being Microsoft 365 rather than security does not make an existing group role-assignable. Role-assignable groups must use assigned membership, so dynamic membership is not allowed.

prompt: A facilities team needs one group that can receive email sent to a single address and can also be granted permissions to a SharePoint site. Which group type meets both needs?

options.text: Mail-enabled security group
Distribution list
Security group
Dynamic distribution list

explanation: A mail-enabled security group has an email address and is also a security principal that can be granted permissions. Distribution lists and dynamic distribution lists are for email only and cannot be used to grant access to resources. A security group can be granted permissions but has no email address.

prompt: The membership of a Microsoft Entra group must always consist of users whose department is Sales. Which dynamic membership rule should be used?

options.text: user.jobTitle -eq "Sales"
user.department -eq "Sales"
device.displayName -eq "Sales"
user.companyName -eq "Sales"

explanation: Dynamic membership rules use the form property, operator, value, so user.department -eq "Sales" selects users whose department is Sales. The rule on user.jobTitle and the rule on user.companyName test different user attributes. The rule on device.displayName would build a device group, and a rule can target users or devices but not both.

prompt: Administrators should hold the Exchange Administrator role only when they need it. An activation must be approved by the security lead before it takes effect. What should be configured in Privileged Identity Management?

options.text: Active assignments, with an access review every quarter
Eligible assignments, with 'require justification on activation' as the only control
Eligible assignments, with approval by the security lead required to activate
Permanent active assignments, with an alert for roles assigned outside PIM

explanation: Eligible assignments require users to activate the role, and the role settings can require approval with a designated approver before activation completes. Active assignments give the role without activation. Justification alone records a reason but needs nobody's approval, and alerts only report on assignments rather than gate them.

prompt: A company plans to use Privileged Identity Management so that 12 administrators have eligible, time-bound role assignments. Which license do these administrators need?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft 365 Copilot
Microsoft Entra ID P2

explanation: Privileged Identity Management requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance for users with eligible or time-bound assignments and for approvers and reviewers. Microsoft Entra ID Free and P1 do not include PIM, and a Microsoft 365 Copilot license is unrelated to identity governance features.

prompt: Policy states that an activated Global Administrator role must expire after at most two hours and that multifactor authentication is required when the role is activated. Where are these requirements set?

options.text: In the Global Administrator role settings in PIM
In the Authentication methods policy
In the group expiration policy
In the properties of an administrative unit

explanation: PIM role settings are configured per role and include the activation maximum duration (1 to 24 hours) and whether MFA, justification, ticket information or approval is required on activation. The Authentication methods policy controls which methods users may register and use. Group expiration applies to Microsoft 365 groups, and administrative units scope role assignments rather than control activation.

prompt: An identity team member must manage Microsoft Entra role assignments in Privileged Identity Management, including making users eligible for roles. Global Administrator must not be used. Which role should be assigned?

options.text: Security Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
User Administrator
Global Reader

explanation: Only Privileged Role Administrator and Global Administrator can manage assignments for Microsoft Entra roles in PIM. Security Administrator manages security features and User Administrator manages users and groups, but neither can assign roles in PIM. Global Reader has read-only access.

prompt: An external auditor needs to view settings across the Microsoft 365 admin centers for two weeks and must not be able to change anything. Which role is appropriate?

options.text: Security Administrator
Service Support Administrator
Global Reader
Helpdesk Administrator

explanation: Global Reader provides read-only access to settings across Microsoft 365 services. Security Administrator can change security settings. Service Support Administrator is focused on service health and support requests rather than broad read access, and Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords.

prompt: A person on the collaboration team will manage Microsoft 365 Copilot settings and other AI-related services for the tenant. This person must not be able to assign user licenses or manage users. Which role fits?

options.text: Global Administrator
License Administrator
User Administrator
AI Administrator

explanation: The AI Administrator role manages all aspects of Microsoft 365 Copilot and AI-related enterprise services but does not manage user licensing. Global Administrator is far broader than needed. License Administrator and User Administrator can assign licenses, which the requirement forbids, and they do not manage Copilot settings.

prompt: A regional help desk must be able to reset passwords only for users in the company's European offices. The tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P1. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create an administrative unit of European users and scope a password-reset role to it
Create a security group of European users and assign the Helpdesk Administrator role to the group
Create a Conditional Access policy that limits help desk sign-ins to European locations
Create a dynamic membership group of European users and make the help desk staff its owners

explanation: Administrative units restrict a role assignment, such as Helpdesk Administrator or Password Administrator, to the users that are members of the unit. Assigning the role to a group would give the group's members that role across the whole tenant. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions, not administrative scope, and group ownership does not grant the right to reset members' passwords.

prompt: A security group named Lab-Staff is added to an administrative unit. A User Administrator who is scoped to that unit can manage the group itself but cannot reset the passwords of the users in the group. Why?

options.text: The User Administrator role cannot be scoped to an administrative unit
Adding a group to an administrative unit does not add its members to scope
Administrative units cannot contain groups
The users must first be removed from all other administrative units

explanation: When a group is added to an administrative unit, only the group object is in scope; its members must be added to the unit as users to be managed by scoped administrators. User Administrator is one of the roles that can be scoped to a unit. Administrative units can contain users, groups and devices, and a user can belong to more than one unit.

prompt: Accounts of executives must be protected so that tenant-level administrators such as User Administrators and Helpdesk Administrators cannot reset their passwords or modify them; only administrators explicitly assigned at the scope of a specific unit may do so. What should be created?

options.text: A role-assignable group that contains the executives
A dynamic membership group with a rule for executive job titles
A restricted management administrative unit that contains the executives
A Conditional Access policy that blocks administrators from the executives' accounts

explanation: In a restricted management administrative unit, only administrators assigned at that unit's scope can modify its members; tenant-level administrators are blocked. Membership of a role-assignable group protects accounts in a different way and is intended for role assignment. A dynamic group gives no protection, and Conditional Access governs sign-ins rather than which administrators may modify directory objects.

prompt: An existing administrative unit contains the finance users. The company now wants it to be a restricted management administrative unit. What must the administrator do?

options.text: Edit the unit's properties and turn on restricted management
