Matches are already occurring, so licensing is not the cause, and whether administrators can see labels in their apps has no effect on alerting.

prompt: A DLP rule generates an alert for every single match and analysts are overwhelmed. They want one alert only when a user causes at least five matches within 60 minutes. What should the administrator change?

options.text: Switch the policy from enforcement to simulation mode
Raise the confidence level of every sensitive information type in the rule from medium to high
Remove the policy tip from the user notification settings
Configure the rule to alert when activity matches a threshold over a time window

explanation: Rule alert settings can aggregate matches and raise an alert only when a threshold, such as a number of matched activities within a number of minutes, is reached. Simulation mode stops enforcement altogether rather than tuning alert volume. Raising confidence levels changes what counts as a match and could hide genuine incidents, and policy tips are user-facing notifications that are unrelated to administrator alerts.

prompt: An analyst can open Microsoft Purview DSPM and see AI activity in Activity explorer, but the text of users' prompts and Copilot's responses is not shown. Which role does the analyst need?

options.text: Data Security AI Viewer
Data Security AI Content Viewer
Global Reader in Microsoft Entra ID
Security Reader

explanation: The Data Security AI Content Viewer role provides read-only access to the prompts and responses of AI interactions. Data Security AI Viewer and the Security Reader role group give view-only access to the pages but explicitly not to prompt and response content. Global Reader can view configuration across services but does not expose the content of AI interactions.

prompt: A company has deployed agent instances that are managed by Microsoft Agent 365. The data security team wants to see which agents were active in the last 30 days and which are associated with risky activity such as oversharing. Where should they look?

options.text: The Reports page in DSPM for AI (classic)
The Alerts page in Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
The AI observability page in Microsoft Purview DSPM
The Content explorer page in Microsoft Purview

explanation: The AI observability page in the current version of DSPM lists agents with activity in the last 30 days, prioritised by risk level, with details and remediation recommendations for each agent. The classic version of DSPM for AI does not support Agent 365. DLP Alerts shows policy-match alerts only, and Content explorer shows where sensitive or labelled items are stored.

prompt: The data security team wants Microsoft Purview DSPM to show when users visit third-party generative AI websites and paste sensitive information into them from Windows devices. Which prerequisites are required?

options.text: Devices onboarded to Microsoft Purview and the Microsoft Purview browser extension deployed
Microsoft 365 Copilot licences assigned to the users and web search in Copilot turned on for all of them
A Copilot connector created for each of the generative AI websites
Sensitivity labels enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive

explanation: Visibility into third-party AI sites relies on endpoint signals, so devices must be onboarded to Microsoft Purview and the Purview browser extension must be deployed where it is required. Copilot licences and web search concern Microsoft 365 Copilot, not other vendors' websites. Copilot connectors index external content for Copilot, and enabling labels in SharePoint and OneDrive affects files stored there rather than browser activity.

prompt: Before a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout, the data security team wants a report of SharePoint sites where content is shared too broadly and contains sensitive information, with suggested fixes. Which Microsoft Purview capability should they use?

options.text: Communication compliance policies
Records management file plan
Compliance Manager improvement actions
Data risk assessments in DSPM

explanation: Data risk assessments in DSPM identify potential oversharing by scanning sites for sensitive content and how it is shared, and they offer remediation options. Communication compliance reviews messages for conduct and regulatory issues. The file plan manages retention labels for records, and Compliance Manager tracks actions against regulations rather than analysing site-level sharing.

prompt: Microsoft 365 Copilot has been in use for a month, but the AI activity views in Microsoft Purview DSPM show no Copilot interactions. Other Purview solutions work. What should the administrator check first?

options.text: That a retention policy exists for the Copilot interactions location
That Microsoft Purview Audit is turned on for the organisation
That every user has a sensitivity label policy published to them
That a Copilot connector has been deployed for SharePoint

explanation: DSPM activity views are built on audit events, so Microsoft Purview Audit must be enabled for Copilot interactions to be captured and displayed. A retention policy controls how long interactions are kept, not whether activity is reported. Label policies are not a prerequisite for activity data, and SharePoint content is available to Copilot without a connector.

prompt: A company has bought Microsoft 365 Copilot licences but has not assigned them. The administrator wants to see which users are on an eligible Microsoft 365 Apps update channel and which unlicensed users are suggested candidates for a pilot. Which report should be used?

options.text: The Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness report under Reports > Usage in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The Microsoft 365 Apps usage report under Reports > Usage in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The data access governance reports in the SharePoint admin center
The Adoption Score people experiences report under Reports > Adoption Score in the Microsoft 365 admin center

explanation: The Copilot readiness report (the Readiness tab of the Copilot report under Reports > Usage) shows prerequisite licences, users on an eligible update channel and a 'Suggested candidate for Copilot' column. The Microsoft 365 Apps usage report shows app activity but no Copilot eligibility. Data access governance reports deal with SharePoint sharing, and Adoption Score measures how people use Microsoft 365 rather than Copilot readiness.

prompt: The Copilot readiness report shows that many users have 'No' in the 'Uses eligible update channel' column. Their devices receive Microsoft 365 Apps updates twice a year. What should the administrator do to make these users ready for Copilot in the desktop apps?

options.text: Assign the users a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and wait 72 hours
Enable the Copilot Frontier setting for the users
Move the devices to Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel
Turn on the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy for the users

explanation: The readiness report counts users as eligible when their devices are on Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel, so the devices need to be moved to one of those channels. Assigning a licence does not change the update channel on the device. Copilot Frontier controls access to preview features, and the web search policy controls grounding in web content; neither affects app update eligibility.

prompt: An administrator is choosing 200 pilot users for Microsoft 365 Copilot and sorts the readiness report by the 'Suggested candidate for Copilot' column. What does a 'Yes' in this column indicate?

options.text: The user has asked for a Copilot licence through a self-service request that is waiting for administrator approval
The user is in the top 25% of unlicensed users by usage of Microsoft 365 apps where Copilot adds value
The user's manager already has a Copilot licence assigned
The user's OneDrive contains no overshared files

explanation: The column flags the top 25% of users without a Copilot licence based on their consistent use of apps such as Teams and Outlook over the preceding period, and the list is re-evaluated weekly. It is not driven by licence requests or by a manager's licence. The report has no information about oversharing in OneDrive; that is assessed with SharePoint and Purview tools.

prompt: An administrator opens the Copilot readiness report to plan licence assignment, but the User name column shows anonymised values instead of user principal names. What should be changed?

options.text: Assign the Reports Reader role to the administrator's account and sign in to the admin center again
Switch the report timeframe from 28 days to 180 days
Export the report to a .csv file and open it in Excel
Change the Reports setting in Org settings to display concealed user, group and site names

explanation: User-specific details are hidden in usage reports by default, and the Reports setting under Org settings controls whether concealed user, group and site names are shown. Reports Reader allows viewing the reports but does not reveal concealed names. Changing the timeframe or exporting the data keeps the same anonymised identifiers.

prompt: An HR SharePoint site was shared with 'Everyone except external users' years ago. Until permissions are cleaned up, the administrator wants the site's content to stop appearing in Microsoft 365 Copilot responses and organisation-wide search for most users, without changing who can open the files. What should be configured?

options.text: Restricted content discovery on the site
A site-level retention policy on the site
A sensitivity label with a watermark on the site's files
Read-only mode on the site through a site lock

explanation: Restricted content discovery in SharePoint Advanced Management keeps a site's content out of Copilot answers and organisation-wide search unless the user owns or recently interacted with it, and it leaves permissions unchanged. A retention policy only controls how long content is kept. A watermark is a visual marking, and locking the site read-only stops edits but the content remains discoverable.

prompt: A finance site contains files that were individually shared with people across the company. The site owner wants only members of the Finance security group to be able to open anything on the site, regardless of earlier sharing. Which control should the SharePoint administrator apply?

options.text: Restricted content discovery
A default sharing link type of 'Specific people'
A restricted access control policy
An inactive site policy

explanation: Restricted access control limits access to a site to members of specified groups, so users outside the group lose access even to files that were shared with them. Restricted content discovery only hides content from Copilot and search and leaves access intact. Changing the default link type affects new links only, and an inactive site policy handles sites that are no longer used.

prompt: Before licensing users for Copilot, the SharePoint administrator needs a list of sites where files were shared through 'Everyone except external users' or organisation-wide sharing links in the last 28 days. Which tool provides this?

options.text: The Copilot readiness report in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Data access governance reports in the SharePoint admin center
The Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The network connectivity insights page in the Microsoft 365 admin center

explanation: Data access governance reports, part of SharePoint Advanced Management, identify sites with potentially overshared content, including sharing-link and 'Everyone except external users' activity. The Copilot readiness report covers licences and update channels. The Copilot usage report measures adoption, and network connectivity insights concern network performance.

prompt: A data access governance report lists 40 sites with broad sharing. The SharePoint administrator does not know which permissions are still needed and wants each site owner to check and confirm or remove access. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Apply Preservation Lock to the sites
Block downloads on the sites with a Conditional Access policy
Convert each site to a hub site
Initiate a site access review from the report

explanation: A site access review, started from a data access governance report, asks site owners to review the flagged sharing and remove what is not needed. Preservation Lock relates to retention policies and does not exist for site permissions. Blocking downloads restricts unmanaged devices but leaves the oversharing in place, and hub sites are a navigation and branding construct.

prompt: During a legal dispute, counsel asks for all Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses of one employee from the past three months. How should the compliance team obtain them?

options.text: Run an eDiscovery search with the employee's mailbox as the data source and filter for Copilot activity
Export the per-user table of the Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report for the employee from the admin center
Open the employee's OneDrive and export the Copilot folder from the recycle bin
Request the data from the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights

explanation: Copilot prompts and responses are stored in the user's mailbox, so an eDiscovery case that searches that mailbox with a condition for Copilot activity returns them for review and export. The usage report contains counts and dates, not conversation content. Interactions are not kept as files in a OneDrive folder, and the Copilot Dashboard shows aggregated adoption and impact metrics.

prompt: An assessment finds hundreds of SharePoint sites that nobody has used for two years. Their outdated content could still ground Microsoft 365 Copilot responses. The administrator wants owners to be notified and asked to confirm, archive or delete these sites automatically. Which feature should be used?

options.text: A DLP policy for the SharePoint sites location
A Copilot connector with a full crawl schedule
An inactive site policy in SharePoint Advanced Management
A Microsoft 365 group expiration policy in Microsoft Entra ID

explanation: The inactive site policy in SharePoint Advanced Management's site lifecycle management detects unused sites and notifies owners to take action. A DLP policy looks for sensitive information rather than inactivity. Copilot connectors bring external content into Microsoft 365, and a group expiration policy applies only to Microsoft 365 groups and not to all SharePoint sites.

prompt: A company wants licensed users to keep web grounding when they use Copilot in Web mode, but Copilot responses in Work mode must never use web content. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Set 'Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office' to Disabled for all licensed users in Cloud Policy service
Enable 'Allow web search in Copilot' with the option that disables Work mode and enables Web mode and Copilot Chat
Turn off Copilot image generation under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions
Ask users to turn off the Web content toggle in their Copilot settings

explanation: The 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy offers a third option: disabled in Work mode, enabled in Web mode and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Disabling optional connected experiences turns off web search everywhere and restricts many other experiences. Image generation is unrelated to web grounding, and relying on a user toggle does not enforce the requirement.

prompt: An administrator follows the web search link on the Copilot settings page and needs to create the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy. Where is this policy created?

options.text: In a Conditional Access policy in the Microsoft Entra admin center
In the Search & intelligence settings under Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center
In a meeting policy in the Teams admin center
In Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365, in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center

explanation: The 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365, which is managed in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions, not Copilot grounding. Search & intelligence manages Microsoft Search answers and connectors, and Teams meeting policies control meeting features.

prompt: In a commercial tenant, the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy has never been configured. The policy 'Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office' is set to Disabled for all users. What is the result for web search in Copilot?

options.text: Web search is unavailable, and other optional connected experiences are restricted as well
Web search stays available because only the dedicated web search policy is able to turn it off
Web search is available in Work mode only and unavailable in Web mode
Web search is available until users switch off the Web content toggle

explanation: When the dedicated policy is not configured, web search is available unless optional connected experiences are disabled, so here web search is off and many other experiences are restricted too. The dedicated policy is the preferred control but not the only one that can turn web search off. There is no outcome where only Work mode keeps web search, and the user toggle is dimmed when an administrator has turned web search off.

prompt: A state agency uses Microsoft 365 GCC. Users report that Microsoft 365 Copilot never includes web content. No Copilot-related policies have been configured. What should the administrator do to allow web grounding?

options.text: Set 'Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office' to Enabled
Assign the users to the Copilot Frontier program
Enable the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy in Cloud Policy service
Opt in to Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor

explanation: In GCC and DoD, web search is off by default and stays off until the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy is enabled. In these environments the optional connected experiences policy does not turn web search on. Copilot Frontier provides preview features, and the AI provider setting controls which models are available rather than web grounding.

prompt: A privacy officer asks what leaves the Microsoft 365 service boundary when Microsoft 365 Copilot uses web search for a prompt that references an internal strategy document. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: The entire document is sent to Bing so that it can be compared with public pages
A generated query of a few words is sent to Bing without the user's Microsoft Entra identifiers
The full prompt and the user's principal name are sent to Bing for personalisation
Nothing is sent to Bing because web results are retrieved from the tenant's own index

explanation: Copilot generates a short search query informed by the prompt and sends it to the Bing search service with identifying information based on the user's Microsoft Entra ID removed. Entire Microsoft 365 files are not included in the query, and the full prompt is not sent unless it is very short. Web grounding does call the Bing search service, so it is wrong to say nothing is sent.

prompt: An administrator sets 'Allow web search in Copilot' to the option that disables web search in Work mode but leaves it enabled in Web mode and Copilot Chat. Which additional effect should the administrator expect?

options.text: Copilot Search stops returning results from Copilot connectors
Users lose access to Copilot in Word, Excel and PowerPoint
The Copilot AI disclaimer is hidden in Work mode
Web search is disabled in Researcher and in Cowork

explanation: With that option selected, web search in Researcher and Cowork is disabled as well, because they operate with work data. Copilot connectors and Copilot Search are not governed by the web search policy. Access to Copilot in the Office apps is determined by licensing and app policies, and the AI disclaimer is a separate setting.

prompt: A company has Microsoft 365 E3 for all users and Microsoft 365 Copilot licences for 500 of them. The administrator is asked what must be configured so that the licensed users get Microsoft 365 Copilot Search. What is the correct answer?

options.text: Nothing; Copilot Search appears as a tab in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app for users with an eligible Copilot licence
A search vertical must be created for each content source before the Search tab appears in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app for licensed users
A Copilot connector must be deployed because Copilot Search only searches external data
The users must be added to a spending policy that includes Copilot Search

explanation: Copilot Search needs no setup by administrators or users: it shows up in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app for anyone with an eligible Copilot licence, at no extra cost. Verticals are a Microsoft Search configuration and are not required. Copilot Search covers Microsoft 365 content as well as connector content, and it is not a usage-based service governed by spending policies.

prompt: Employees often type 'travel booking' into Copilot Search. The administrator wants the official travel portal to appear as an authoritative result at the top for that query. What should be created?

options.text: A retention label for the travel portal site
An acronym answer
A bookmark answer
A Copilot connector for the travel portal

explanation: Bookmarks are curated answers that promote key resources for chosen keywords, and they are surfaced in Copilot Search results. Acronym answers define terminology rather than promote a link. A retention label has nothing to do with search results, and a connector indexes external content but does not pin a specific link to the top for a keyword.

prompt: New employees keep asking what 'QBR' and 'OKR' mean inside the company. The administrator wants Copilot Search to return the company's own definitions when users search for these terms. What should be configured?

options.text: Bookmark answers with the terms as reserved keywords
Acronym answers in the Microsoft Search settings
A custom dictionary under Copilot > Settings > Other settings
A Copilot AI disclaimer with a link to the glossary

explanation: Acronym answers let administrators define terminology used in the workplace, and Copilot Search shows these curated answers. Bookmarks promote resources and links rather than definitions. The Copilot custom dictionary manages vocabulary for supported Teams experiences such as transcription, and the AI disclaimer only adds a notice to Copilot responses.

prompt: A company has deployed a ServiceNow Copilot connector. Licensed users search in Microsoft 365 Copilot Search and unlicensed users search in Microsoft Search. What difference should the administrator expect for the connector content?

options.text: Neither experience can show connector content until a result type is designed
Only Microsoft Search can show connector content, because Copilot Search is limited to Microsoft Graph data from Microsoft 365 workloads
Both experiences require the content to be added to the Restricted SharePoint Search allowed list
Copilot Search supports tenant-enabled connectors immediately; Microsoft Search needs a vertical configured for the connector

explanation: Copilot Search provides instant support for all tenant-enabled connectors with semantic search, while Microsoft Search requires administrators to set up verticals and result types for connector content to appear. Copilot Search covers both Microsoft Graph and third-party connector data. Restricted SharePoint Search relates to SharePoint sites, not connector content, and a result type is not a prerequisite for Copilot Search.

prompt: A company wants employees to be able to start a Microsoft 365 Copilot trial on their own, but they must not be able to buy licences without going through procurement. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Set Microsoft 365 Copilot self-service purchases to allow trials only, under Copilot > Settings > User access
Turn off 'Microsoft Copilot in admin centers' under Copilot > Settings > User access
Remove the Copilot service plan from every user's licence on the Licenses page under Billing in the admin center
Create a spending policy with a credit limit of zero under Copilot > Cost Management

explanation: The self-service purchases setting under User access has three choices: allow trials and purchases, allow trials only, or do not allow, so 'trials only' fits exactly. 'Copilot in admin centers' controls whether administrators can use Copilot in admin portals. Removing service plans disables Copilot for existing licences, and spending policies govern usage-based services rather than self-service licence purchases.

prompt: A security review concludes that the helpdesk administrators should not be able to use the Copilot experience that is built into the Microsoft 365 admin center. Where does an AI Administrator control this?

options.text: Agents > Settings > User access in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Copilot > Settings > User access > Microsoft Copilot in admin centers
Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy > Privileged access
Roles > Role assignments in the Microsoft 365 admin center

explanation: The 'Microsoft Copilot in admin centers' setting under Copilot > Settings > User access manages whether eligible administrators can use Copilot in supported admin centers. Agents > Settings > User access controls who can use agents and plugins. Privileged access relates to approval workflows for privileged tasks, and role assignments define administrative permissions rather than access to this Copilot experience.

prompt: A regulated company wants every Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat response to carry a notice that AI output may be inaccurate, with a link to the company's own AI usage policy. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A sensitivity label with a footer content marking that is published to all users as the default label
A mail flow rule that appends a disclaimer to messages
A custom request policy with a redirect URL under Cost Management
The Copilot AI disclaimer setting under Copilot > Settings, with a custom policy link

explanation: The Copilot AI disclaimer setting (found via View all on the Copilot settings page) turns on a disclaimer in Copilot and lets the administrator supply a custom link; leaving the link blank keeps Microsoft's default. Sensitivity label markings apply to documents and emails, not to Copilot responses. Mail flow rules affect email only, and request policies redirect Copilot credit requests.

prompt: A company's brand team does not want employees to create AI-generated images with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Which setting should the administrator turn off?

options.text: Screen and camera sharing under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions
Advanced package uploads under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions
Copilot image generation under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions
Pin Copilot Chat under Copilot > Settings > User access

explanation: Copilot image generation is a dedicated setting under Copilot actions that allows or prevents supported image-generation experiences. Screen and camera sharing manages Copilot Vision. Advanced package uploads controls who can upload agent and plugin packages, and Pin Copilot Chat only affects navigation placement.

prompt: An IT department wants a group of 30 champions to try eligible Microsoft 365 Copilot features before they reach general availability, while everyone else stays on released features. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: The Copilot Frontier setting, scoped to the champions group
A Copilot connector that is staged to the champions group
The 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy for the champions group
A second Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for each champion

explanation: Copilot Frontier (Copilot > Settings > View all) lets the administrator choose which users or groups can access eligible preview features before general availability. A connector rollout only controls who sees connector content. The web search policy controls grounding, and a user cannot gain preview features by holding a second licence.

prompt: A change-averse organisation wants newly released, generally available Microsoft 365 Copilot features to reach its users later than the default schedule, so that the service desk can prepare. Which Copilot release preference should the administrator select?

options.text: Standard release
Deferred release
Copilot Frontier
Monthly Enterprise Channel

explanation: The Copilot release preferences for general availability offer Standard release, which is the default, and Deferred release, which delays generally available features. Copilot Frontier does the opposite by giving early access to preview features. Monthly Enterprise Channel is an update channel for the Microsoft 365 Apps on devices, not a Copilot release preference.

prompt: A help desk lead must be able to change settings on the Copilot > Settings page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The company follows least privilege. Which role should be assigned?

options.text: Global Reader
Global Administrator
Service Support Administrator
AI Administrator

explanation: AI Administrator is the appropriate role for managing Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Global Reader can view the settings but not change them. Global Administrator would work but violates least privilege, and Service Support Administrator is intended for service health and support requests.

prompt: Legal wants to prevent employees from using AI video generation in Microsoft 365 Copilot and supported apps until a policy review is finished. Where should the administrator control access to this capability?

options.text: In a Teams meeting policy in the Teams admin center
In the Stream settings of the SharePoint admin center
In the Copilot settings of the Microsoft 365 admin center
In an Endpoint DLP policy in the Microsoft Purview portal

explanation: The Microsoft 365 admin center includes a Copilot setting that lets administrators control access to AI video generation features in Microsoft 365 Copilot and supported apps. Teams meeting policies control recording and transcription of meetings, not Copilot video generation. SharePoint admin settings govern where videos are stored, and Endpoint DLP governs how sensitive files are handled on devices.

prompt: After Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is rolled out, the administrator wants the Chat entry to be pinned in the navigation of supported Microsoft 365 apps for everyone, so users do not have to pin it themselves. Where is this configured?

options.text: Copilot > Settings > User access > Pin Copilot Chat
Agents > All agents > Manage pinned agents
Settings > Integrated apps > Deployed apps
Teams admin center > Setup policies > Pinned apps

explanation: The Pin Copilot Chat setting under Copilot > Settings > User access controls whether Chat is pinned in supported app navigation. Manage pinned agents controls which agents are pinned inside Copilot, not the Chat entry itself. Integrated apps deploys add-ins and apps, and a Teams setup policy only pins apps inside Teams.

prompt: A company does not want users to create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks yet. How should the administrator turn these experiences off?

options.text: Block the Loop app under Agents > All agents
Turn off the Pages and Notebooks setting under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions in the admin center
Remove the SharePoint service plan from the users' licences
Configure the applicable Cloud Policy settings for Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

explanation: Whether users can create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks is managed with Cloud Policy settings, not on the Copilot settings page. Blocking an agent in the registry does not control Pages or Notebooks. The Copilot actions section has no toggle for them, and removing SharePoint would break far more than these two features.

prompt: New company laptops have a Copilot key on the keyboard. The administrator wants to control what the key opens on managed Windows devices. How should this be done?

options.text: With the Pin Copilot Chat setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center
With Windows policies or the Microsoft Intune settings catalog
With a Conditional Access policy that targets the Copilot app
With an agent management rule under Agents > Settings

explanation: The Copilot hardware key is managed through supported Windows policies or the Intune settings catalog. Pin Copilot Chat only affects navigation inside Microsoft 365 apps. Conditional Access governs sign-in to resources rather than keyboard behaviour, and agent management rules apply bulk actions to agents.

prompt: An administrator turns off the 'Screen and camera sharing' setting under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions. Which statement describes the effect on users of the Microsoft 365 Copilot app?

options.text: Copilot can no longer be used in Teams meetings that are recorded
Users can no longer upload image files to Copilot Chat prompts
Copilot Vision is turned off, but voice conversations with Copilot remain available
Both Copilot Vision and voice conversations with Copilot are turned off

explanation: The Screen and camera sharing setting manages Vision in Copilot, and turning it off does not turn off voice. Copilot in Teams meetings is managed in the Teams admin center. The setting is not described as blocking file uploads to prompts, and it is specifically documented as not affecting voice.

prompt: A company wants 50 project managers to use Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork. Everyone already has a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, but Cowork is not available to anyone. What must the administrator do?

options.text: Enable usage-based billing and create a spending policy that includes the project managers and selects Cowork
Select the Cowork entry under Agents > All agents and deploy it to the project managers as specific users or groups
Assign the project managers a Microsoft Agent 365 licence in the Licenses page
Add the project managers to the Copilot Frontier setting under Copilot > Settings

explanation: Cowork access is granted through usage-based billing: users must be in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork. The Cowork entry under All agents is still visible, but configuring it no longer has any effect on access. Agent 365 licences are for agent governance, and Frontier controls preview features rather than access to the generally available Cowork.

prompt: Finance asks the administrator to stop one contractor from using Copilot Cowork. The contractor is covered by two spending policies that include Cowork. Which action removes the contractor's access?

options.text: Set the contractor's per-user credit limit to the lowest value in both policies
Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor for the contractor
Block the Cowork entry under Agents > All agents for the contractor
Remove the contractor from every spending policy that includes Cowork

explanation: A spending policy is an access control as well as a budget, so the user has to be removed from every spending policy that selects Cowork. A low credit limit does not block access. Turning off Anthropic models changes which models are available but not whether Cowork can be used, and the agent entry under All agents no longer controls access.

prompt: During the preview, a company allowed Cowork for a pilot group by configuring the Cowork agent entry under Agents > All agents. After general availability, the administrator must keep the same people enabled. What should be done?

options.text: Nothing; the allow list on the agent entry continues to control access
Re-upload Cowork as a custom agent and publish it to the pilot group
Put the pilot users in a security group and scope a spending policy that selects Cowork to that group
Create an access package for the pilot users in Microsoft Entra entitlement management and assign it directly

explanation: The agent-based control from the preview is deprecated; at general availability access comes only from a spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork, so the old allow list should be re-expressed as a security group scoped in a policy under Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration. The agent entry no longer has any effect. Cowork is not a custom agent that can be uploaded, and access packages do not grant Cowork access.

prompt: Users want Copilot Cowork to complete tasks on websites in Microsoft Edge on their own devices. The capability is not available in the tenant. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Deploy a Copilot connector for each website the users need
Turn on the Cowork Browsing tenant setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Enable the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy for all users
Approve a bring-your-own MCP server request under Agents > Tools

explanation: Whether Cowork can use the local browser is governed by the Cowork Browsing tenant setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Copilot connectors index external content and do not let Cowork operate a browser. The web search policy only controls grounding with Bing results, and MCP server approvals make tools available to agents.

prompt: A company in the United States turns off Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor. Users who are covered by a spending policy that includes Cowork ask whether they can still use Cowork. What is the outcome?

options.text: Cowork keeps working and Auto selects from the remaining models the organisation allows
Cowork is blocked until a Global Administrator re-enables Anthropic
Cowork keeps working but only for scheduled prompts, not interactive tasks
Cowork is blocked until each of the users is assigned a Microsoft Agent 365 licence by an administrator

explanation: Model settings control which models users see, not whether they can use Cowork; with the Anthropic family off, Cowork continues with the non-Anthropic models and Auto picks from what remains. Access itself is determined by the spending policy, so nothing has to be re-enabled. There is no restriction to scheduled prompts, and Agent 365 licences are unrelated to Cowork access.

prompt: A UK-based organisation wants its users to be able to choose Claude models in Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences. The option is currently unavailable to users. What should an AI Administrator do?

options.text: Create an 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy in Cloud Policy service
Add Anthropic as an enterprise application in the Microsoft Entra admin center and grant tenant-wide admin consent
Upload the Claude model as a custom agent under Agents > All agents
Enable Anthropic under 'AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors' in the Copilot settings

explanation: For tenants in the EU, EFTA and the UK the Anthropic subprocessor setting defaults to off, and an AI Administrator or Global Administrator opts in under Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. The web search policy has nothing to do with model providers. Registering an enterprise application or uploading an agent does not enable Claude models in Copilot.

prompt: A US company keeps Anthropic enabled as a Microsoft subprocessor, but only the research department should be able to use Copilot features that rely on Claude models. How should this be achieved?

options.text: Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks the Anthropic service for all users outside the department
Publish a sensitivity label that only the research department can apply
In the AI provider setting, limit access to Anthropic models to the research security group
Create a DLP policy for the Copilot location that excludes the research department

explanation: Access to an AI provider subprocessor can be assigned to specific users or Microsoft Entra security groups in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and the assignment is enforced across Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences. Conditional Access cannot target the model provider used inside Copilot. Sensitivity labels and DLP policies protect content rather than select who may use a model provider.

prompt: An administrator notices a separate setting named 'AI providers operating as independent processors'. An engineering team wants an advanced Anthropic model that is listed there as requiring data retention. What should the administrator understand before enabling it?

options.text: It is covered by Microsoft's Product Terms and Data Protection Addendum like the other Claude models that Microsoft offers
It is off by default everywhere, and enabling it means accepting Anthropic's own terms because Anthropic stores the data
It is enabled automatically for any user who is in a spending policy that includes Cowork
It can only be enabled from the Power Platform admin center by a Power Platform Administrator

explanation: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default for all scenarios; the tenant administrator must explicitly opt in, accept Anthropic's commercial terms and data protection addendum, and choose which users get access, because Anthropic acts as an independent processor and retains data outside the Microsoft agreement. They are therefore not covered by Microsoft's Product Terms and DPA. Spending policies do not enable them, and the opt-in is made in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

prompt: Anthropic has been enabled as a Microsoft subprocessor in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Makers report that they still cannot use Anthropic models for their agents in Copilot Studio. Where should the administrator look next?

options.text: The additional controls for external models in the Power Platform admin center
The Agent and plugin access setting under Agents > Settings
The Search & intelligence settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center
The data access governance reports in the SharePoint admin center

explanation: Once the provider is enabled in the Microsoft 365 admin center, additional admin controls in the Power Platform admin center determine whether Anthropic models can be used in Copilot Studio and Power Platform. Agent and plugin access controls which publisher categories of agents users can install. Search & intelligence and SharePoint governance reports are unrelated to model availability.

prompt: A company wants content from its ServiceNow knowledge base to be available in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Which role and location should be used to set this up with least privilege?

options.text: SharePoint Administrator, in the SharePoint admin center under Policies
Teams Administrator, in the Teams admin center under Manage apps
Compliance Administrator, in the Microsoft Purview portal under Data connectors
AI Administrator, in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Connectors

explanation: Copilot connectors are deployed from Copilot > Connectors (Gallery) in the Microsoft 365 admin center by an AI administrator. The SharePoint and Teams admin centers do not host Copilot connectors. Purview data connectors import third-party data for compliance purposes, not for grounding Copilot.

prompt: While configuring a Copilot connector for a wiki, the administrator must make sure that Copilot shows each article only to people who can read it in the wiki itself. Which setting on the Users tab of Custom setup should be chosen?

options.text: Everyone in the organization
Only users with access to the content
A staged rollout to a subset of users
A semantic label mapped to the title property

explanation: Under Access permissions, 'Only users with access to the content' makes the indexed items visible only to users who have access in the source, using identity mapping to Microsoft Entra ID. 'Everyone in the organization' would expose every indexed article to all users. A staged rollout limits who can see the connection during validation, and semantic labels improve relevance rather than security.

prompt: A team's access to several folders was removed in the source system of a Copilot connector three days ago, yet the former members still get that content in Copilot. Incremental crawls run every 15 minutes. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Increase the frequency of the incremental crawl to every five minutes
Change the access permissions setting to 'Everyone in the organization'
Run a full crawl, because incremental crawls do not process permission updates
Delete the semantic labels and assign them again on the Content tab

explanation: Incremental crawls pick up new and changed items but do not process permission changes, so a full crawl is needed to update access control lists. A more frequent incremental crawl would still ignore the permission change. Making the content visible to everyone would worsen the exposure, and semantic labels have no effect on permissions.

prompt: An administrator is creating a new Copilot connector for a document management system and wants a small group to validate the results before the content becomes available to the whole company. What should be done during setup?

options.text: Deploy the connector to a subset of users first and expand the rollout after validation
Create the connection in simulation mode and review the matched items in Activity explorer first
Set the full crawl recurrence to monthly until validation is complete
Mark every property as refinable so that testers can filter the results

explanation: The connector setup lets the administrator deploy the connection to a subset of users for validation before a broader rollout. Simulation mode and Activity explorer belong to Microsoft Purview policies, not connectors. A slow crawl schedule delays indexing for everyone without limiting visibility, and schema attributes such as refinable control search behaviour rather than audience.

prompt: Several agent identities are sponsored by employees in the sales department. When a sponsor leaves the company, sponsorship must pass automatically to that person's manager so that every agent identity keeps an accountable human. What should the identity administrator configure?

options.text: A leaver lifecycle workflow that includes the 'Transfer agent identity sponsorships to manager' task
A joiner lifecycle workflow that includes the 'Generate Temporary Access Pass and send via email to user's manager' task
An access review of the sales department's Microsoft 365 groups
A Conditional Access policy that targets the departing users

explanation: Lifecycle Workflows provide agent sponsor tasks, including 'Transfer agent identity sponsorships to manager', which can run in a leaver workflow so that sponsorship moves to the sponsor's manager. A joiner workflow with a Temporary Access Pass task onboards new users and does not touch sponsorships. Access reviews of groups and Conditional Access policies do not reassign agent sponsors.

prompt: An administrator creates a lifecycle workflow from a joiner template and cannot find the tasks 'Send email to manager about sponsorship changes' or 'Send email to co-sponsors about sponsor changes'. Why?

options.text: The tasks require the Global Administrator role to be visible in the Microsoft Entra admin center
The tasks are created with Microsoft Graph PowerShell only
The tasks are mover and leaver tasks and are only offered in templates of those categories
The tasks appear only after a custom task extension is registered with an Azure Logic App

explanation: All three agent sponsor tasks are classified as mover and leaver tasks, so they can only be selected in workflows based on mover or leaver templates. Visibility of the tasks is not tied to Global Administrator, and they can be added in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Custom task extensions call external logic apps and are not required for built-in tasks.

prompt: A company follows least privilege. Which Microsoft Entra role should be assigned to the person who will create lifecycle workflows that handle agent identity sponsor changes?

options.text: AI Administrator
Privileged Authentication Administrator
Global Administrator
Lifecycle Workflows Administrator

explanation: Creating workflows in ID Governance > Lifecycle workflows requires at least the Lifecycle Workflows Administrator role. AI Administrator manages Copilot and agent settings in Microsoft 365, not lifecycle workflows. Privileged Authentication Administrator manages authentication methods, and Global Administrator would work but is not least privilege.

prompt: An audit asks how the tenant deals with agent identities that are created and then never used again. No custom governance has been configured. What does Microsoft Entra Agent ID do by default?

options.text: It deletes every agent identity 30 days after it is created
It identifies inactive agent identities, notifies relevant users and then disables the identity
It converts inactive agent identities into service principals without sponsors
It does nothing until an administrator creates an access review or a lifecycle workflow for agents

explanation: Microsoft Entra Agent ID provides a default inactivity policy to all tenants that identifies inactive agent identities, notifies relevant users and then disables the identity if there is still no activity. It does not delete identities on a fixed 30-day timer. Agent identities are not converted to service principals, and the default policy exists without any access review being configured.

prompt: An identity governance administrator builds an access package that grants a security group membership and a Microsoft Graph permission. Agent identities must be able to receive it. Which choice in the assignment policy makes this possible?

options.text: For users, service principals, and agent identities in your directory, with the All agents option
For users not in your directory, with the All connected organizations option
None (administrator direct assignments only), with a custom extension
For users in your directory, with the All members (excluding guests) option and one approval stage

explanation: In the 'Who can get access' section, selecting 'For users, service principals, and agent identities in your directory' and then 'All agents' allows agent identities to request the access package. The option for users not in your directory is for external users. Direct assignment only would block requests by agents and their sponsors, and 'All members' covers human users only.

prompt: A compliance rule states that an AI agent must never obtain additional access without a named human asking for it. The agent has an agent identity with a sponsor, and an access package is available for agents. How should access be requested?

options.text: The agent calls Microsoft Graph to create its own access package assignment request whenever it needs more access
The agent's blueprint inherits the access package automatically at creation
The agent's sponsor requests the access package on behalf of the agent identity in the My Access portal
A Conditional Access policy assigns the access package when the agent signs in

explanation: A sponsor can request an access package on behalf of the agent identity from the My Access portal, which provides human oversight for the request. The agent identity can also request programmatically, but that would not satisfy the requirement for a named human requester. Blueprints pass on inheritable permissions rather than access packages, and Conditional Access controls conditions of access rather than assigning packages.

prompt: An autonomous agent runs every night with no signed-in user and calls Microsoft Graph with its own agent identity. The security team wants to block it whenever Microsoft Entra ID Protection rates the agent as high risk. How should the Conditional Access policy be assigned?

options.text: To all users, with the user risk condition set to high
To the agent identity, with the agent risk condition set to high
To the agent identity blueprint principal's owner, with sign-in risk set to high
To all guest users, with the device platform condition set to any

explanation: In the application-only pattern the token is issued to the agent identity, so the policy must target the agent identity (or its blueprint) and can trigger on agent risk. A policy for all users with user risk only evaluates human sign-ins. The blueprint owner's sign-in risk and guest device platforms have no bearing on an agent acquiring tokens with its own identity.

prompt: A project uses twelve agent identities that were all created from one agent identity blueprint, and more will be added. One Conditional Access policy must apply to all of them, including future ones, with no further edits. What should the policy target?

options.text: A security group that contains the agents' user accounts
Each of the twelve agent identities, selected individually
The users who sponsor the agent identities
The agent identity blueprint

explanation: A policy that targets an agent identity blueprint applies to all agent identities created from that blueprint, including ones created later. Scoping by group membership of agents' user accounts is not supported, and it would not cover the agent identities anyway. Selecting identities individually requires an edit for every new agent, and targeting sponsors only affects the humans' own sign-ins.

prompt: An agent has its own agent user account with a mailbox and a Teams licence. An existing Conditional Access policy applies to 'All users' and blocks access from outside trusted locations, but sign-in logs show it is not applied to the agent's user account. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a policy that is assigned to Agents and targets the agent users
Add the agent's user account to a group and include the group in the existing policy
Enable security defaults so that the block applies to every identity
Assign the existing policy to the agent identity blueprint

explanation: Policies scoped through the Users assignment, including All users and groups, do not apply to agents' user accounts; a policy must be created under 'Users, agents, or workload identities' > Agents that targets agent users. Scoping agent user accounts by group membership is not supported. Conditional Access policies do not apply when security defaults are enabled, and a blueprint-targeted policy covers agent identities, not the agent's user account.

prompt: An interactive agent accesses SharePoint files on behalf of the signed-in employee. The security team wants multifactor authentication to be required before the agent can get a token for SharePoint. Which identity should the Conditional Access policy target?

options.text: The agent identity, because it requests the token
The agent identity blueprint, because it defines the agent
The users, because the signed-in user is the token subject in the on-behalf-of flow
The agent's sponsor, because the sponsor is the person accountable for the agent's access

explanation: In the on-behalf-of (delegated) flow the signed-in user is the token subject, so Conditional Access evaluates policies assigned to that user, and the token exchange is evaluated as well. Selecting the agent identity or its blueprint as the policy subject does not cover requests made on behalf of a user. The sponsor has a governance role and is not part of the token request.

prompt: Forty agents built with Agent Builder have become ownerless because their creators left the company. The administrator wants to hand all of them to the former owners' managers in one operation. What should be used in the Microsoft 365 admin center?

options.text: The Manage pinned agents action on the Registry page
The agent management rule that reassigns ownerless agents to the manager
The Export action followed by a .csv import of new owners
The Agent feedback sharing setting under Agents > Settings

explanation: Agent management rules under Agents > Settings include a rule that reassigns ownerless Agent Builder agents to the manager of the previous owner in bulk, after the administrator reviews the affected agents. Manage pinned agents only controls which agents are pinned for users. Export produces a list but there is no import of owners, and feedback sharing controls whether developers receive ratings and comments.

prompt: The owner of a shared Copilot Studio agent has moved to another division. An administrator selects the agent under Agents > All agents and uses 'Assign new owner'. What happens to the previous owner?

options.text: The previous owner keeps read access to the agent and its files
The previous owner becomes a co-owner with the same rights as the new owner
The previous owner keeps edit rights until the next publish of the agent
The previous owner loses all access, including read rights

explanation: After reassignment the new owner gets full edit and delete permissions plus access to files the previous owner uploaded, and the previous owner loses all access, including read rights. Read access is not retained. Co-ownership is not created by this action, and there is no grace period tied to the next publish.

prompt: A department wants a second person to share responsibility for an Agent Builder agent. The administrator opens the Owners pane for the agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Which statement is correct?

options.text: An individual user can be added as an owner, and all owners have the same rights
A Microsoft 365 group can be added as an owner so that membership changes apply automatically
A secondary owner can be added with read-only rights to the agent
The last remaining owner can be removed to make the agent ownerless on purpose

explanation: Agent Builder agents support multiple owners; owners must be individual users, and every owner has the same rights to edit, share and manage the agent. Groups are not supported as owners. There are no primary or secondary owner roles, and the last remaining owner cannot be removed.

prompt: In Microsoft Entra Agent ID, a sponsor disabled an agent identity by mistake and now wants it working again. The sponsor has no administrator role. Who can re-enable the agent identity?

options.text: The sponsor, from the My Access portal
The manager set on the agent's user account
An owner of the agent identity or an administrator
Any member of the group that sponsors the blueprint

explanation: Sponsors are limited to non-destructive lifecycle operations such as disabling or soft-deleting and cannot re-enable or restore; an owner or an administrator must do that. The My Access portal is for requesting access packages. Managers cannot modify agents, and members of a sponsor group have sponsor rights only.

prompt: A security policy forbids the use of agents and plugins from publishers outside Microsoft and the company itself. Users should not find such agents in the store. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Under Agents > Settings > Sharing, select 'No users'
Under Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access, clear the option for agents and plugins built by external publishers
Under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions, turn off advanced package uploads for every user and group in the organisation
Under Agents > Settings > Agent feedback sharing, select 'No agents'

explanation: Agent and plugin access controls which categories of agents and plugins users can view and install: Microsoft, your organisation and external publishers; disabling the external option removes those from the store. Sharing governs how users share Agent Builder agents. Advanced package uploads controls who can upload packages, and feedback sharing only affects whether developers receive feedback.

prompt: An administrator sets the Sharing option under Agents > Settings to 'No users'. Which statement describes the result?

options.text: No agent of any type, including Copilot Studio and SharePoint agents, can be shared or published in the tenant any more
Copilot Studio agents can no longer be submitted for admin approval
Agents that were already shared are deleted after 30 days
Organisation-level sharing of Agent Builder agents is off, but users can still share with specific individuals

explanation: The Sharing control applies only to agents built with Agent Builder; 'No users' disables sharing at organisation level while users can still share directly with specific people. It does not stop sharing or publishing of other agent types. Copilot Studio submissions go through the Requests flow, and the setting does not delete existing agents.

prompt: During a phased rollout only members of the 'AI Pilots' group may use agents and plugins. Other users who already have agents installed must not be able to use them either. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Agents > Settings > User access, set to specific users or groups with 'AI Pilots' selected
Agents > All agents > Manage pinned agents, pinned for 'AI Pilots'
Agents > Settings > Tags, with an 'AI Pilots' tag on every agent
Agents > Settings > Sharing, set to specific users or groups with the 'AI Pilots' group selected

explanation: The User access setting decides who can use agents and plugins; with 'Specific users or groups', only the selected users can use them even if others are able to install agents from the registry. Pinning only makes agents more visible. Tags are labels for organising agents, and Sharing controls who may share Agent Builder agents rather than who may use agents.

prompt: An administrator wants a custom policy template for agents that includes a Conditional Access policy. When adding the template under Agents > Settings > Templates, the Conditional Access policy cannot be selected. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Templates can contain Microsoft Purview policies only
The policy is in report-only mode, which templates do not accept
The policy has not been created in Microsoft Entra with at least one agent identity selected
The policy was created by a Global Administrator instead of by an account with the AI Administrator role

explanation: Custom template policies must first be created in Microsoft Entra, and only Conditional Access policies that include at least one agent identity are visible when a template is created in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Custom templates are specifically for Microsoft Entra policies such as Conditional Access, access packages and custom security attributes. Report-only state is not documented as a blocker, and AI Administrators actually lack the privileges to configure Conditional Access.

prompt: A custom policy template was applied when ten agents were activated. The administrator later edits the template and adds an access package policy. What is the effect on the ten agents?

options.text: They receive the new policy at their next sign-in
They are not affected; the updated template applies only to new activations
They are blocked until an administrator approves them again
They are moved to the Microsoft default template automatically

explanation: An updated template applies to all new activations and does not change agents that are already approved. Existing agents do not pick up template edits at sign-in. They are neither blocked nor moved to the default template because of the edit.

prompt: An administrator maintains tags so that agents can be organised by business unit. The tenant has reached the tag limit, and the administrator plans to delete the 'Legacy' tag, which is on 35 agents. What should the administrator know?

options.text: The limit is 500 tags, and deleting a tag blocks the agents that use it until they are retagged
The limit is 100 tags, and a tag in use cannot be deleted
The limit is 25 tags, and deleting a tag deletes the agents that use it
The limit is 50 tags, and deleting a tag removes it from every agent that uses it

explanation: An organisation can have up to 50 tags, and deleting a tag removes it from every agent that uses it, so the agent count should be checked first. Deleting a tag neither blocks nor deletes agents. A tag that is in use can be deleted, which is exactly why the warning exists.

prompt: An administrator needs a list of every agent in the tenant that was built with Copilot Studio in order to review them. Where can this be obtained in the Microsoft 365 admin center?

options.text: Agents > All agents > Registry, filtered by Platform
Copilot > Connectors > Gallery, filtered by Source
Settings > Org settings > Services, filtered by Workload
Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot, filtered by Readiness

explanation: The agent Registry under Agents > All agents lists all agents available to the organisation, and the Platform filter shows which product was used to create each agent. The connector gallery lists data-source connectors. Org settings holds service configuration, and the Copilot report shows readiness and usage rather than an agent inventory.

prompt: In the agent registry, the same Copilot Studio agent appears in two rows: one with the publisher type 'Shared by creator' and one with 'Published by your org'. The administrator suspects a synchronisation error. What is the correct interpretation?

options.text: The agent was uploaded twice and one of the packages should be deleted
The rows indicate a version conflict that the maker must resolve in Copilot Studio before publishing
The rows are separate lifecycle and publisher records for the same agent and are expected
The agent was copied to a second Power Platform environment

explanation: A Copilot Studio agent can appear more than once with different publisher types; these rows represent separate lifecycle and publisher records for the same underlying agent and are by design. It is not a duplicate upload, and removing one entry does not remove the other. It does not indicate a version conflict or a copy in another environment.

prompt: The summary at the top of the agent registry shows a number for 'Unmanaged agents'. What does this number represent?

options.text: Agents that have been blocked by an administrator
Agents created or managed outside of Agent 365, without its risk protection and observability
Agents whose owners have left the organisation
Agents that were submitted by makers and are waiting for an administrator to review and publish them

explanation: 'Unmanaged agents' counts agents that are created or managed outside of Agent 365 and therefore lack its risk protection and observability. Blocked agents are a status, not this card. Agents whose owners left are counted under 'Agents without owners', and agents awaiting review are listed on the Requests tab.

prompt: A sales manager wants the 'Deal Coach' agent to appear prominently in Microsoft 365 Copilot for the sales team. The administrator opens Manage pinned agents, but 'Deal Coach' cannot be pinned. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The agent was built by an external publisher, not by Microsoft
The agent has more than one owner
The agent has no tags assigned
The agent is not deployed to any users, or it is blocked

explanation: Only deployed agents can be pinned, and a blocked agent has to be unblocked first, so the agent must be deployed to the sales team before it can be pinned for them. Publisher type does not prevent pinning. The number of owners and the presence of tags are irrelevant to pinning.

prompt: A developer packages a custom agent with the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit and submits it to the organisation. The administrator has reviewed its data sources and permissions and wants to make it available to the HR department only. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Under Agents > All agents > Requests, select the agent, choose 'Publish to store' and select the HR users in the wizard
Under Settings > Integrated apps, upload the package again and assign it to HR
Under Agents > Settings > Sharing, choose 'Specific users' and select HR
Under Copilot > Settings > Data access > Agents, add the HR department's security group to the list of allowed users and select Save

explanation: Submitted agents appear in the Requests list, and 'Publish to store' starts a wizard in which the administrator selects the users or groups, applies a policy template and reviews permissions. Uploading the package again is unnecessary because the submission is already pending. The Sharing setting applies to Agent Builder agents, and the request is not approved from the Copilot settings page.

prompt: A developer publishes an update to an agent that is already available in the organisation. The update appears in the Requests list with the state 'Pending update'. What do users experience until the administrator acts?

options.text: The agent is unavailable until the update is approved
Users are asked to choose between the two versions
Users continue to use the previous version of the agent
The update is applied automatically after 30 days

explanation: Until the administrator approves the update with 'Update in store', users can access the previous version of the agent. The agent is not taken offline while the update is pending. Users are not offered a choice of versions, and there is no automatic approval after a waiting period.

prompt: A Microsoft-built agent is blocked in the tenant. A user opens it in the store and selects Request. The request appears with the state 'Allow user to install'. What must the administrator do to grant the request?

options.text: Reject the request and ask the user to install the agent from Teams instead
Unblock the agent, then select the request and choose Approve
Assign the user a Microsoft Agent 365 licence, then choose Approve
Upload the agent as a custom agent, then deploy it to the user

explanation: A banner reminds the administrator that a blocked agent must be unblocked before any request to install it can be accepted; after unblocking, the request can be approved. Installing from Teams would hit the same block. The request workflow does not depend on an Agent 365 licence for the user, and a Microsoft-built agent is not re-uploaded as a custom agent.

prompt: A maker hands the administrator a .zip package downloaded from Copilot Studio. The agent should be manageable in the tenant inventory and preinstalled for the support team. What should the administrator do?

options.text: In Copilot > Connectors, add the package as a custom connector and stage the rollout to the support team
In Agents > Tools > Registry, select Upload and scope it to the support team
In the Teams admin center, add the package to a setup policy for the support team
In Agents > All agents, select Add agent, upload the .zip file and choose the support team under Deploy

explanation: The Add agent action on the All agents page uploads an agent manifest package (.zip); the wizard lets the administrator choose who can install it under Publish and who gets it preinstalled under Deploy, and apply a policy template. Copilot connectors are for external data sources. The Tools registry upload is for plugins and skills, and the documented path for custom agents is the Microsoft 365 admin center upload.

prompt: Management wants the Researcher agent to be available to the strategy team only. The administrator finds that the 'Edit users' panel for Researcher is disabled. What does this mean for the requirement?

options.text: The agent can only be made unavailable by blocking it for the entire tenant
The agent must first be deleted and then added again with a narrower audience
The agent can be scoped once a custom policy template has been applied
The agent can be scoped by adding a tag for the strategy team

explanation: For the Researcher and Analyst agents the Edit users panel is disabled, and their availability is managed by blocking the agent for the whole tenant with the Block action. First-party agents like this are not deleted and re-added. Policy templates apply governance policies, and tags are organisational labels; neither scopes availability.

prompt: An administrator deletes a Copilot Studio agent from the Microsoft 365 admin center. Two weeks later the business asks for it back. What can the administrator do?

options.text: Nothing; deletion in the admin center is permanent and immediate
Open a support request, because only Microsoft can restore a deleted agent
Restore the agent from the Deleted view, because it is soft deleted for 30 days
Ask the maker to republish, because deletion only removes the registry entry

explanation: Deleting an agent is a soft delete: its properties and resources are retained for 30 days, during which it can be restored from the Deleted view with its previous configuration. Deletion is therefore not immediately permanent, and no support request is needed. The delete makes the agent unavailable to its maker and users rather than only removing a registry row.

prompt: An administrator must stop the compute resources behind a Microsoft Foundry agent from the Microsoft 365 admin center because of a cost overrun. The Stop action is not available to the administrator. What is required?

options.text: The Teams Administrator role
The Azure AI Owner role
The Global Reader role
The Lifecycle Workflows Administrator role

explanation: Start and Stop act on the underlying Azure infrastructure of a Foundry agent and require the Azure AI Owner role, which can be added from the agent details pane. Teams Administrator and Lifecycle Workflows Administrator have no rights over Azure compute. Global Reader is a read-only role.

prompt: An MCP server registered on Agent 365 exposes six tools. Five are read-only, and one issues refunds. The administrator wants agents to keep using the read-only tools while the refund tool is unavailable. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Reject the server under Agents > Tools > Requests and ask the developer to register it again without the refund tool
Clear the external publishers option under Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access
Block the whole MCP server on the Registry tab under Agents > Tools
Open the server on the Registry tab under Agents > Tools and disable the refund tool on its Tools tab

explanation: Tool-level granular control lets the administrator turn individual tools of a supported MCP server on or off on the server's Tools tab, and the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces it at runtime. Blocking the whole server disables all six tools. Rejecting the registration removes the server entirely, and Agent and plugin access controls publisher categories rather than individual tools.

prompt: A developer registers a remote MCP server and the registration appears under Agents > Tools on the Requests tab. An AI Administrator selects Approve, but agent builders still cannot use the server an hour later. What step is most likely missing?

options.text: Consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions that the MCP server requires
Assignment of a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to the MCP server
Publication of a sensitivity label policy to the developer
Creation of a spending policy that includes the MCP server

explanation: Approval and consent are separate steps: after approving the registration, the administrator must consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions the server requires, and only then does it become available to agent-building surfaces. MCP servers are not licensed with Copilot licences. Sensitivity label policies and spending policies play no part in making a registered server available.

prompt: A company runs its MCP servers behind Azure AI Gateway and wants them discovered automatically on the Tools page of the Microsoft 365 admin center. An AI Administrator cannot complete the connection under Agents > Settings > Gateways. Why?

options.text: The gateway can only be connected from the Azure portal
The connection requires an Agent 365 licence for every MCP server
Connecting Azure AI Gateway requires the Global Administrator role
Each MCP server must be approved individually before the gateway connects

explanation: Connecting Azure AI Gateway to Microsoft 365 must be done by a Global Administrator; the AI Administrator role does not support this operation. The connection is made in the Microsoft 365 admin center, not the Azure portal. Consent is given once per tenant and applies to all MCP servers in the connected gateway, so servers are not approved one by one, and MCP servers are not licensed individually.

prompt: An administrator blocks a plugin package under Agents > Tools > Plugins. The package includes two agents and uses an MCP server that another plugin also uses. What is the effect?

options.text: The package, its agents and the shared MCP server are all blocked, including for the other plugin that uses the server
The package and its included agents are blocked, while the shared MCP server stays available to other plugins
Only the package is blocked; its included agents remain available to users
The package is uninstalled and permanently deleted from the registry

explanation: Blocking a plugin prevents access to the plugin and its included agents because they share the same governance controls, while associated MCP servers and connectors remain available to other plugins. Blocking the MCP server itself is a separate component-level action. The included agents do not stay available, and blocking does not delete the package; unblocking restores access.

prompt: An operations manager asks how many hours of work the organisation's agents performed last month. Which metric on the Agents > Overview page in the Microsoft 365 admin center answers this?

options.text: Agent run-time
Active users
Agent registry
Registry sync

explanation: Agent run-time is the total hours worked by agents during the last 30 days, measured from when a request begins until it completes and aggregated across agent activities. Active users counts unique people who interacted with at least one agent. Agent registry is the total number of agents in the catalogue, and Registry sync shows the external platforms that were scanned.

prompt: A company activated Microsoft Agent 365 licences ten days ago. On the Agents > Overview page, the Active users and Agent run-time figures for its third-party agents look far lower than expected for a 30-day period. What explains this?

options.text: Third-party agents are never included in these metrics
The metrics for third-party agents are refreshed only once every 30 days after activation
Data collection for third-party agents starts when Agent 365 licences are activated
The administrator needs the Global Reader role to see third-party data

explanation: For third-party agents, data collection begins at Agent 365 licence activation, so the 30-day metrics reflect fewer days until enough activity has accumulated. Third-party agents are included once licences are active. The metrics are not on a 30-day refresh cycle, and a reader role does not change which data is collected.

prompt: The 'Top actions for you' area of the Agents > Overview page shows a card named 'Agents with exceptions' with a count of 7. What does the card indicate?

options.text: Seven agents are excluded from the default policy template
Seven agents have errors in their conversations
Seven agents are exempt from Conditional Access policies
Seven agents have pending publish requests

explanation: The 'Agents with exceptions' card shows the number of agents that have errors in their conversations, and View details opens a filtered list of those agents. It does not relate to exclusions from templates or from Conditional Access. Pending publish requests are shown on the 'Pending requests for agents' card.
